issuers.issuingEntity: Not named. ToS: "PreStocks is a distributed network of contributors located around the world who collaborate primarily through digital means." No incorporated issuer, SPV sponsor or counterparty is identified anywhere in the public materials.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: unknown - undisclosed. ToS states components "may be operated, performed, or provided by different legal entities in different jurisdictions" and that the entity contracting with the user "may differ between products, tokens, jurisdictions, and points in time, and may be added, removed, substituted, restructured, or replaced at any time without notice".
issuers.governingLaw: British Virgin Islands law. ToS s.“Governing Law and Jurisdiction”: all matters and disputes "shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the British Virgin Islands". Note the BVI is simultaneously on the Prohibited Jurisdictions list. Disputes go to good-faith negotiation for 30 days, then binding arbitration under the London Court of International Arbitration Rules; seat London, England; sole arbitrator; English language; individual basis only (no class actions), with the courts of the British Virgin Islands taking exclusive jurisdiction over any claim for which the class-action waiver is held unenforceable. What is still missing is the counterparty, not the law: no issuing entity or jurisdiction of incorporation is named.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: Unlicensed and self-disclaiming. Site disclaimer: "PreStocks is not a broker-dealer, investment advisor, exchange operator, transfer agent, custodian, virtual asset service provider, or similar regulated entity." No securities registration or exemption is cited; the ToS instead asserts "All blockchain transfers via the Services are secondary transfers effected outside the United States and are not primary offerings to U.S. persons" (Regulation S-style posture, but Reg S is never named).
issuers.holderClaim: A bearer Token-2022 token that "reference[s] economic exposure to designated pre-IPO companies" and confers "no ownership, voting, dividend, information, or other legal rights". The ToS grants no proprietary interest in any SPV, share or asset; the holder's only stated entitlement is to request redemption for USDC "or another mutually agreed form of value", which the operator may satisfy instead by pointing the holder at on-chain liquidity.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: Undisclosed by design. FAQ: "Counterparty legal names are not disclosed because they require contractual confidentiality to avoid unwanted solicitation, reputational targeting, and potential adverse actions from issuers or intermediaries." Backing is described only as "one or more vetted holding entities that verifiably own the underlying exposure".

custodyVerification.frequency: "published periodically or available on request if costs are covered" (FAQ) - no cadence committed
custodyVerification.notes: Claimed only. CoinDesk (2026-05-13): "neither the platform nor any third-party auditor has published the attestation reports the company promised at launch." Verified 2026-09-16: /attestations, /transparency, /proof-of-reserve and /reserves all return HTTP 404, and no attestation page appears in sitemap.xml. The only machine-readable feed is the issuer's own unsigned price/supply API.

redemption.eligibility: Any non-US, non-Restricted holder "may request redemption" - discretionary, not an entitlement. Which path is used "depends on those circumstances"; the operator may direct the holder to on-chain liquidity instead of processing a redemption.
redemption.rails: USDC or "another mutually agreed form of value"; alternatively realisation via on-chain liquidity, conversions, wraps, migrations or exchanges. Post-IPO the stated path is conversion into an equivalent tokenized public stock rather than cash.
redemption.fees: Unbounded and unilateral. ToS reserves redemption, settlement, conversion and withdrawal fees plus markups/spreads, enforced "at the token, smart-contract, or program level" via transfer-fee configurations and hooks, changeable "without prior notice and without your consent", with no obligation "to publish, itemize, or explain the basis of any fee". Observed on-chain: 50 bps transfer fee, raised from 0 bps (fee epoch 848 -> 1032).

issuers.corporateActions: IPO: underlying positions become convertible on-chain (without KYC) into an equivalent tokenized public stock; typical 6-month post-IPO lockup during which the token may trade at a discount; holders have 9 months post-IPO (3 months after lockup) to convert, after which "the tokens will expire worthless and will no longer be supported". M&A: cash deals distribute net proceeds pro rata as USDC; equity deals may become convertible into a tokenized version of the acquirer's equity "if we create and support one", with a 6-month conversion window, then expiry. Separately, balances can be restated unilaterally through the scaledUiAmountConfig multiplier, and this has happened twice: SPACEX x5 effective 2026-06-10T04:30:00Z and OPENAI x1.4861347 effective 2026-07-17T16:30:00Z. Which holding entities hold the exposure, and in what form? Names are withheld as policy, so the 1:1 backing claim in the API description is unverifiable in principle, not just in practice.
Is ANTHROPIC exposure backed at all after Anthropic declared SPV transfers void under its transfer restrictions? The token still trades and the supply was never reduced.
Has any attestation report ever been produced to any holder on request, and at what cost?
Why was the OPENAI scaledUiAmount multiplier set to 1.4861347 on 2026-07-17 - a share split at OpenAI, a restatement of units per token, or a correction of over/under-collateralisation?

RESOLVED, kept for the record: the ToS last updated 2026-09-08 does elect a substantive law - the internal laws of the British Virgin Islands - with LCIA arbitration seated in London and BVI courts as the fallback forum. The BVI is also a Prohibited Jurisdiction under the same document. What remains unanswered is who the BVI-law counterparty is.
Why does SPACEX trade about 21% below the issuer's own mark if mint/redeem arbitrage works as the FAQ describes?

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Authority keys in practice, 2026-09-16): one key WV9PJN7XTmTLVwbutCLFxp8TyePee6Xq5mRq6Fti5Wc holds mint, freeze, permanent-delegate, pause, metadata and transfer-fee authority on all 8 mints, and is Squads-multisig-controlled (Squads v4 program seen in its transactions, which are mostly withdrawWithheldTokensFromMint fee harvesting). Multisig on signers, fully concentrated on roles.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Tokens are described in the ToS as "bearer digital tokens"; there is no shareholder register, transfer agent or off-chain holder list, and the operator explicitly disclaims being a transfer agent. Whoever holds the mint's token accounts is the holder. Note this is the ledger for the claim, not for the underlying shares, which sit in an undisclosed holding entity's own books.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Compliance is reactive, not proactive: defaultAccountState is "initialized" (new accounts are not frozen), the transferHook extension carries a null programId, and no allowlist gates transfers. Any wallet can send to any wallet today, subject only to a 50 bps fee. The freeze, pause, clawback and blocklist powers are exercised after the fact, which is exactly the reactiveCompliance model this flag implies.

bearerRedemption.reason: Redemption is a discretionary request, not a bearer right. A holder "may request redemption of Tokens for USDC or another mutually agreed form of value", and whether a redemption is the path used "depends on" operational, legal and market circumstances - the operator may instead point the holder at on-chain liquidity. US persons are excluded entirely, and the counterparty holding the exposure is undisclosed, so there is no identified third party against whom presenting the token compels delivery.

forcedTransfers.reason: Confirmed both in law and on-chain. ToS: tokens are subject to "freezing, forced transfer, burning, refund, compulsory redemption, migration, and the addition of addresses to transfer allowlists or blocklists", and the mints carry a live permanentDelegate plus freeze and pausable authorities all held by WV9PJN7XTmTLVwbutCLFxp8TyePee6Xq5mRq6Fti5Wc. The operator may act "without prior notice and without your consent" and is "under no obligation to investigate before acting".

titleDeed.reason: Explicitly disclaimed: PreStocks "confer no ownership, voting, dividend, information, or other legal rights" and are "not affiliated with, endorsed by, or issued by" the referenced company. The token references economic exposure held by a third party; it is a derived partial right, not title.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Ordinary Token-2022 mints held in any Solana wallet (Phantom, Trust, Bitget and others are listed integrations); no custodial account is required and no KYC gates holding.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token is worthless without the operator. Post-IPO value depends on the operator creating and supporting a tokenized public stock to convert into, and tokens "expire worthless and will no longer be supported" after a 9-month (IPO) or 6-month (M&A) conversion window. The operator can also pause all transfers globally, and the backing counterparties are unnamed, so no holder could pursue them if the operator disappeared.

presetJurisdiction.reason: No issuing entity and no jurisdiction of incorporation are stated; the ToS says the contracting entity may be "added, removed, substituted, restructured, or replaced at any time without notice" and that counterparties need not be publicly identified. The legal frame itself IS fixed - British Virgin Islands law governs, with an LCIA arbitration seat in London and BVI courts as the fallback forum - but a jurisdiction without an identifiable person in it fixes neither the counterparty nor who a holder could sue, which is what this flag is about.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Attestation is promised but nothing exists to attach. Reports are "published periodically or available on request if costs are covered", no attestor is named, CoinDesk reported on 2026-05-13 that none had ever been published, and every plausible transparency URL 404s as of 2026-09-16. There is no on-chain attestation or proof-of-reserve feed.

issuers.issuerText: Remora Markets (formerly Moose Capital; subsidiary of Step Finance) — WOUND DOWN February 2026
products: rStocks / rTokens: Token-2022 tokens on Solana tracking single US equities — TSLAr (Tesla), NVDAr (NVIDIA), CRCLr (Circle), SPYr (SP500), MSTRr (Strategy) and others, live from 2025-09-02

issuers.issuingEntity: unknown. No primary source names a legal issuing entity. The platform was 'formerly Moose Capital', acquired by Step Finance in December 2024 and rebranded; Step Finance said it had integrated Moose Capital's team and regulatory licences. The public site never named a company, and its own Terms & Conditions, Whitepaper and KYC Info pages were published as empty stubs (verified in the Wayback capture of 2025-05-16). Note: 'Remora Capital Corporation' (Maryland, SEC CIK 2045370) is a middle-market credit BDC and is NOT related.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: unknown. The About page claimed only an 'Asset management license in premium offshore jurisdictions' and that 'Custodial services [are] managed by Wealth Management providers regulated in UAE'; secondary reporting says Remora was registered in Canada and the UAE. Circumstantial support for the UAE: app.remora.markets is a CNAME to mooseprodapialb-2015871155.me-central-1.elb.amazonaws.com — an AWS load balancer in the UAE (me-central-1) region, whose name preserves the 'Moose' origin. The CNAME target no longer resolves.
issuers.governingLaw: unknown — never published. The /terms-conditions/ page existed but contained no terms.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: unknown / self-asserted only. Claimed an unnamed offshore asset-management licence and UAE-regulated custodial providers; no regulator, licence number, prospectus or exemption was ever published. The platform was not available to users in the United States or Europe pending approvals, and required KYB for business users.
issuers.holderClaim: Undocumented. In practice the holder held a platform-issued token that the operator asserted was backed 1:1 by the corresponding security or metal held through an unnamed regulated custodian, redeemable through the platform for USDC. No terms, prospectus or note conditions were ever published, so the legal nature, ranking and enforceability of the claim are unknown; post-wind-down the operator characterised it as a USDC redemption claim rather than a claim to the share.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: unknown — never named. The About page said only 'Custodial services managed by Wealth Management providers regulated in UAE'. (A prior claim in the rwa-sonar attestations DB naming BitGo, sourced to https://remoramarkets.xyz/proof-of-reserves, could not be corroborated: that domain does not resolve as of 2026-09-16 and no archived copy of such a page was retrievable.)

custodyVerification.frequency: Claimed 'Monthly Proof of Reserve audits' on the About page; no auditor named, no report ever located
custodyVerification.notes: No proof-of-reserve page, report, feed or oracle was found from any primary source. There is no Chainlink PoR feed, no attestation firm named, and no API. Post-wind-down the operator merely asserted that 'all rTokens are still fully backed at a 1:1 ratio' with no supporting evidence. The claim of monthly third-party PoR audits should be treated as unverified marketing, not an attestation.

redemption.eligibility: Originally: hold a Remora platform account (KYC for individuals, KYB for businesses); deposit USDC to mint, redeem through the platform. Post-wind-down: the operator said it was 'developing a redemption process for holders to exchange for USDC', and on 2026-03-02 deployed exit liquidity on Manifest DEX priced at the prior Friday's market close, reachable through the Jupiter and Titan swap routers — i.e. open to any token holder via a DEX rather than a contractual redemption right.
redemption.rails: USDC on Solana (mint and redeem); post-wind-down, a DEX exit-liquidity pool on Manifest routed via Jupiter/Titan

issuers.corporateActions: unknown. The mints carry the Token-2022 scaledUiAmountConfig extension — the same mechanism xStocks uses for rebasing dividends and splits — but the multiplier is 1 with no scheduled change on every mint inspected (TSLAr, NVDAr, GLDr), so no rebasing had ever been applied. No dividend, split or delisting policy was ever published.

pricing.notes: Minting was priced at 'the current price on traditional exchanges' per the platform's own How It Works page — a platform mark, with no named oracle. Arbitrage depended entirely on the platform's mint/redeem window being open to the arbitrageur, which required an account; that window is now closed. The wind-down exit liquidity was priced off the prior Friday's market close, i.e. a stale mark. CoinGecko's 'Remora Markets Tokenized rStocks' category reports a $138.9M aggregate market cap against RWA.xyz's $1.99M distributed asset value for the same platform on the same date — treat all third-party valuation figures for these tokens as unreliable.

incidents.summary: Parent Step Finance was compromised: attacker access to executive-team devices allowed stake authority on treasury wallets to be transferred, and 261,854 SOL (~$28.9M at the time; ~$40M including fee wallets) was unstaked and moved out of the project's control. STEP fell roughly 96% over the following weeks. This was a parent-treasury compromise, not a compromise of the rToken mints or of customer collateral as far as reported.
incidents.quote: On January 31, 2026, Step Finance disclosed a critical security incident: attacker access to compromised devices belonging to executive team members allowed stake authorization to be transferred from the project's treasury wallets. A total of 261,854 SOL — worth approximately $28.9 million at the time of the theft — was unstaked and moved out of project control.

incidents.summary: Step Finance announced it would wind down all operations immediately after failing to secure financing or an acquisition — the Step dashboard, SolanaFloor and Remora Markets all shut down. Remora stated all rTokens remained fully backed 1:1 and that it was developing a USDC redemption process for holders.
incidents.quote: Remora stated that all rTokens are still fully backed at a 1:1 ratio and is developing a redemption process for holders to exchange for USDC.

incidents.summary: Remora deployed exit liquidity for rToken holders on Manifest DEX, priced at the prior Friday's market close and accessible through the Jupiter and Titan swap routers.
incidents.quote: On March 2, 2026, Remora deployed USDC exit liquidity on Manifest, a Solana order book DEX. That liquidity was immediately available through Jupiter and Titan — the same swap routers users had relied on to acquire the tokens — priced at the prior Friday's market close.

incidents.summary: The remora.markets TLS certificate (Sectigo, CN=remora.markets, issued 2025-03-07) expired and was never renewed. As of 2026-09-16 the apex domain serves a cPanel default placeholder page (/cgi-sys/defaultwebpage.cgi), www.remora.markets has no A record, api./docs. do not resolve, app.remora.markets is a CNAME to an AWS me-central-1 load balancer that no longer resolves, and the alternate domain remoramarkets.xyz does not resolve at all. The Wayback record shows the site had become a bare directory autoindex by 2026-02-25.

openQuestions: What is the actual issuing legal entity and its jurisdiction? Nothing primary names it. Candidate lead: the former 'Moose Capital' entity, with UAE infrastructure (app.remora.markets CNAME to an AWS me-central-1 load balancer named 'mooseprodapialb') and secondary reporting of Canadian and UAE registration — none of which is a filing.

Is the collateral still actually there? The 1:1 backing claim of 2026-02 has never been evidenced, and ~$2M of rTokens across ~3,600 holders is still outstanding as of 2026-09-16. Who now holds the underlying shares and metals, and under what mandate?
Is the exit-liquidity pool on Manifest still funded and quoting, and at what price relative to the underlying? If it is drained, residual holders have no exit at all.

Who controls the key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb after the wind-down, and was it ever in scope of the January 2026 device compromise? It can still freeze, pause, mint and seize every rToken.

Why does CoinGecko's 'Remora Markets Tokenized rStocks' category report a ~$138.9M aggregate market cap with R-prefixed tickers (RTSLA, RCRCL, RGOOGL, RMU, RINTC) when the on-chain mints use r-suffixed tickers (TSLAr, CRCLr) and RWA.xyz reports $1.99M for the same platform on the same date? At least one aggregator is describing something other than these mints, or using stale/unreliable prices.

The brief's premise that Remora is 'listed on Jupiter's stocks tag' no longer holds: as of 2026-09-16 Jupiter's stocks/rwa/equities tags contain xStocks and Ondo tokens, while the rTokens carry only 'community-assist'/'token-2022'/'unknown'. When were they de-tagged, and by whom?
Did Remora ever publish a single proof-of-reserve report? None was found; if one exists it would materially change thirdPartyAttestations.

keyGovernance.evidence: Every rToken mint names the single key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb as mint, freeze, pause, permanent-delegate and metadata authority (RPC getAccountInfo on FJug3z58gssSTDhVNkTse5fP8GRZzuidf9SRtfB2RhDe and the other mints, 2026-09-16; re-verified 2026-09-17). Characterised 2026-09-17: that key is NOT a bare keypair but the Squads v4 vault PDA (vault index 0, bump 251) of multisig 7QsgDVkiM2285Mvi5TUf1gtHj1QzcqMyix6Rgrcqko35, which is owned by the Squads v4 program SQDS4ep65T869zMMBKyuUq6aD6EgTu8psMjkvj52pCf, has threshold 2 of 3 members, timeLock 0 and configAuthority 11111111111111111111111111111111 (no config authority, so membership and threshold are immutable), and had reached transactionIndex 640. Members: 4aog1ZhoEDrx47fddZ1BYq6yeXgb8mufTubJ3dvgLi6f (permissions 3), 7bzfFK9VxtUgK9Pr1mg7HegQtWPk9mXxmXkf556QMAEz (permissions 7), H61gpHmkSvTSLNWDuJvLA62EVtjrdfHDD5hF978pwa4E (permissions 6). Proof it is the vault and not a keypair: in tx 3wLDeSocn6Tg52KPjH3HWvohfpq9vVWoo8d9zXGLiSXd9L1h2BkpJtvYuET8KjurUuNMT1Ls1QEhRhrgsdGHy7Ts (2026-06-29) the Squads program logs 'Instruction: VaultTransactionExecute' and DQSTm2Wt... signs an inner SPL transferChecked as authority, which a transaction-level keypair signature does not do and a PDA can only do by CPI; the vault PDA derivation for index 0 also hashes to that address exactly. So all three powers sit behind a 2-of-3 multisig rather than one key, though the three member identities remain unattributed.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: No legal documentation was ever published — the Terms & Conditions and Whitepaper pages were empty — so nothing establishes whether the chain or the operator's internal books was the authoritative record of entitlement. Evidence cuts both ways: minting and redemption ran through the platform's account system (suggesting an off-chain book), but the wind-down remedy was open DEX exit liquidity honouring whoever held the token (suggesting ledger state governed). Recorded as unknown rather than guessed.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Verified on Solana mainnet 2026-09-16 for TSLAr, NVDAr and GLDr: defaultAccountState = initialized (accounts are not frozen on creation, so no allowlist) and no transferHook extension at all. The platform itself advertised withdrawing rTokens to your own non-custodial wallet and using them across Solana DeFi. No gatekeeper approval was required for a transfer.

bearerRedemption.reason: Minting and redemption both ran through a Remora platform account subject to KYC (KYB for businesses); holding the token alone never entitled the bearer to the underlying. After the wind-down the only route out is a discretionary exit-liquidity pool on a DEX, priced off a stale mark — a courtesy, not a redemption right, and with no published terms there is nothing to enforce.

forcedTransfers.reason: Verified on-chain: every rToken mint carries a permanentDelegate, a freezeAuthority and a pausableConfig, all set to the single key DQSTm2WtpKBdpKx9t2cYL9Ja8fe7v4yEVEtA7NnSsdqb (which is also mint authority, metadata update authority and scaledUiAmount authority). Whoever holds that key can move or burn any holder's tokens without consent. Concentration in one key is itself a risk given the parent's January 2026 device compromise.

titleDeed.reason: The token was marketed as economic exposure to a stock or metal held by a third-party custodian, not as the security itself. No shareholder rights, no register entry, no published instrument conveying ownership.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: The platform's How It Works page instructed users to 'Withdraw your RWAs to your own non-custodial wallet on Solana', and on-chain state confirms ordinary unfrozen Token-2022 accounts. Self-custody works and still works today.

issuerIndependent.reason: Demonstrated empirically, not merely inferred: the issuer wound down in February 2026 and the token's meaning collapsed with it. The web presence is gone (apex domain serves a cPanel placeholder, TLS expired 2026-03-06, alternate domain does not resolve), no proof of reserves is published, no redemption counterparty is contactable, and residual holders are left with a token whose backing rests on an undocumented assertion. The tokens still transfer, but they no longer reliably mean anything.

presetJurisdiction.reason: No governing law, forum or issuing entity was ever disclosed. The strongest published statement was 'Asset management license in premium offshore jurisdictions' with no jurisdiction, regulator or licence named, and the Terms & Conditions page was blank. A holder cannot determine which law governs the claim or where to bring it.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: 'Monthly Proof of Reserve audits' were claimed on the About page but no auditor was ever named, no report was ever published, and no feed or oracle existed. No independent attestation was attached to the token in any form. (The earlier rwa-sonar record asserting BitGo custody, sourced to remoramarkets.xyz/proof-of-reserves, is unsupported — that domain does not resolve.)

aiReady.reason: Per the vocabulary formula: unconditionalTransfers = yes and tokenSelfCustody = yes, so no KYC sits in the transfer loop and an agent could hold and trade rTokens. Largely academic now — with the issuer gone, there is nothing worth holding.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The on-chain mechanism exists (permanent delegate, freeze, pause) but there is no published governing law, no named entity, no forum and no operator still answering — so there is no route by which a court decision could be directed at anyone with the power to act on the ledger. issuers.name: Republic Mirror
issuers.issuerText: RepublicX LLC — a Delaware LLC formed in 2025 (SEC CIK 0002080279, offices 149 5th Ave Floor 10 / 149 23rd Street #1314, New York, NY 10010), manager OpenDeal Inc. (the Republic group parent), sole named director Jeffrey Vier. RepublicX is described by Republic as 'the innovation arm of Republic primarily in the business of providing asset tokenization services'. THE REFERENCED COMPANIES ARE NOT THE ISSUER AND ARE NOT INVOLVED: 'rSPAX Mirror Notes are not issued by, sponsored by, or affiliated with SpaceX. SpaceX has not reviewed, endorsed, or participated in this offering in any capacity.' This is categorically different from the Bullish/Securitize/Superstate cases — there is no issuer-sponsored tokenization of anything here, and no transfer agent, because there is no share register.
chains: Solana — stated by Republic as the chain for Mirror Tokens: 'The rSpaceX token will be minted on the Solana blockchain using a Republic-created security token asset standard.' NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: no mint address was located and no on-chain state was read, so rwa-sonar cannot confirm from the chain that any genuine Mirror Note token exists on Solana mainnet, nor when it was minted, nor its supply.
products: Mirror Notes / 'Mirror Tokens' — unsecured debt notes issued by RepublicX LLC designed to mirror the economic outcome of holding shares in a named private company, minted on Solana 'using a Republic-created security token asset standard'
rSpaceX / rSPAX — the first and flagship offering, announced 2025-06-25, referencing SpaceX; minimum $50, maximum initial purchase $5,000, payable by Apple Pay or stablecoin

Announced or listed follow-ons referencing other private companies: the republic.com/mirror grid names 24 reference companies with per-card statuses - SpaceX "Live now"; Perplexity, Anthropic and Epic Games "Filled"; Canva, Databricks, Ramp and others "Reservations open"; plus OpenAI, Revolut, Cursor, Anduril, Mercury, Hugging Face, Blue Origin, xAI, Neuralink, Airtable, Linear, Waymo, Replit, Discord, Notion, Telegram and Figure AI. Figma, which the dossier previously listed, is not in the grid, though Republic’s own FAQ says "Future Mirror Tokens may include companies like Figma, Epic Games, Anduril, and more." Only the SpaceX offering appears on EDGAR.

Republic Europe (formerly Seedrs) offers 'RepublicX Mirror Notes' to UK/EU investors under a separate, non-SEC regime — a parallel distribution channel that must not be conflated with the US offerings
issuers.issuingEntity: RepublicX LLC, Delaware limited liability company, year of incorporation 2025, principal place of business New York, NY. Manager: OpenDeal Inc. (149 5th Ave Floor 10, New York, NY 10010). Director/signatory: Jeffrey Vier. Related group entities on EDGAR: Republic Core LLC (CIK 0001794805, SIC 6199, Reg CF issuer of the Republic Note, files Form C-AR annual reports — its 2026 C-AR and C-AR/A are the only EDGAR documents whose full text mentions 'Mirror Token'). There is NO transfer agent, NO registrar and NO custodian named for the Mirror Notes anywhere in the sources located.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Delaware LLC, operations New York, USA. UK/EU distribution runs through Republic Europe under its own regime.
issuers.governingLaw: US federal securities law for the two exempt offerings (Reg CF s.4(a)(6) and Rule 506(c) - see regulatoryStatus) plus, presumably, Delaware LLC law and New York law for the note instrument. PARTLY VERIFIED NOW: republic.com and europe.republic.com still return HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) from this host, but the Internet Archive was reachable on 2026-09-17, so the offering pages have been read from Wayback snapshots. That yields the exemptions, the payout formula and Reference Price, the 10-year maturity, the Qualified Liquidity Event definition, the acceleration remedy on an Event of Default, the senior-unsecured ranking, the keepwell agreement of OpenDeal Inc., the fee architecture and the transfer restrictions. What is STILL unread is the note itself: the subscription agreement, the Note, the payout formula in full, the keepwell terms and the governing-law clause of the instrument are all "described in the Notes and the Offering Documents", which are behind the investment checkout.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: TWO CONCURRENT EXEMPT OFFERINGS OF THE SAME NOTE, one of whose filings cannot be found. The rSPAX offering page presents them side by side. (1) "All US Residents" - Regulation CF: "This securities offering is being conducted pursuant to the exemption from registration afforded under Section 4(a)(6) of the Securities Act of 1933 (“Regulation Crowdfunding”)", "conducted by RepublicX, LLC (the “Issuer”) via OpenDeal Portal LLC d/b/a Republic, an SEC registered funding portal", minimum $50, maximum $5,000, intermediary "Republic Funding Portal". (2) "US Accredited & Global Investors" - Rule 506(c): "Under Regulation D, participation is limited to verified accredited investors in the United States", minimum $50, no broker-dealer involved ("No broker-dealer registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”), the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (“FINRA”), or any state securities regulator is participating in, or has otherwise passed upon or approved this offering") and no SIPC protection. So the Form D on EDGAR - exemption item 06c, security type DEBT, first sale 2025-11-28, $585,205 of $3,500,000 sold, 199 investors, hasNonAccreditedInvestors FALSE, offering closed - is the 506(c) leg, and the accredited-only data is consistent rather than contradictory. THE REMAINING PROBLEM IS A MISSING FILING, NOT A MISMATCHED ONE: the Reg CF panel states "The Issuer has filed a Form C with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”), which contains important information about this offering and its risks", and no Form C exists. EDGAR company search returns exactly one CIK for "RepublicX" (0002080279) whose complete filing history is Form D and Form D/A; EDGAR full-text search returns 4 hits for "RepublicX" (those two filings plus two Republic Core LLC Form C-ARs), 0 for "rSpaceX" and 0 for "Contingent Payout Note". Separately, the /mirror page’s "rule 206 of Regulation CF" citation is a testing-the-waters reservation notice, not the offering itself: it says in terms that "No investment commitments can be accepted and no funds can be received unless the issuer files a Form C with the SEC and starts accepting investments." (3) NOT A REGISTERED SECURITY on any view: no registration statement, no exchange listing, no transfer agent. (4) The UK/EU channel is separately regulated: the rSPAX Mirror Notes campaign on Republic Europe was "approved by Seedrs Limited (trading as Republic Europe) ... as of 17 September 2025 as a financial promotion", and Republic Europe "is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority with firm reference number 550317".
issuers.holderClaim: A SENIOR UNSECURED DEBT CLAIM ON REPUBLICX LLC, with a parent keepwell behind it and nothing else. The instrument is named on the offering page: "You are purchasing tokenized interests in Contingent Payout Notes (each, a “Note”, and if multiple “Notes”), a debt security (i.e., payment obligation) issued by RepublicX". It bears no interest ("There is no periodic interest on the Notes"), matures 10 years from issuance, and pays "a pro rata portion of the value of a common share of SpaceX at that time" on the earlier of maturity or a Qualified Liquidity Event. On default: "the entire unpaid principal of the Securities shall become immediately due and payable at the option of the Investor. As senior unsecured creditors of RepublicX LLC, Investors’ claims to the assets of RepublicX LLC will have priority over those of RepublicX LLC’s equity holders." REPUBLICX HOLDS NOTHING AGAINST IT, and says so: "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset. Instead, offering proceeds are used for RepublicX’s general corporate purposes", and the notes are "subject to repayment from funds available to RepublicX from its business and operations and not from any dedicated pool of investor proceeds". The one piece of credit support is a parent undertaking whose terms are not published: "Your sole counterparty is RepublicX LLC, which alone, aside from that certain keepwell agreement of OpenDeal Inc., as discussed in the Offering Documents, is responsible for all payment and reporting obligations under the Notes." The holder owns no share, no equity, no fund unit and no interest in any SPV: "You have no right whatsoever to equity in SpaceX, RepublicX, or Republic by virtue of investing in any offering." The referenced company is not a party.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: NONE, now on the issuer’s own words rather than by inference. The rSPAX offering page states that "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset", that proceeds go to "RepublicX’s general corporate purposes ... primarily technology and product development, platform and operating costs (including services from affiliates), payroll, and related working capital, and may be reallocated in management’s discretion", and that the notes are repaid "from funds available to RepublicX from its business and operations and not from any dedicated pool of investor proceeds". So there is no custodian, trustee, collateral agent or SPV because there is nothing to custody. The only party holding anything for investors sits on the UK/EU channel, where "Seedrs will act as Custodian rather than provide our standard nominee service" - a custodian of the investment position on Republic Europe’s books, not of any SpaceX exposure.

custodyVerification.notes: THERE IS NO VERIFICATION SURFACE AT ALL, ON-CHAIN OR OFF - and as of 2026-09-17 that is confirmed against the issuer’s own offering pages, not merely unfound. No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release, or on republic.com/mirror, republic.com/rspax or the Republic Europe campaign page (all three read from Wayback snapshots on 2026-09-17 after the live URLs again returned HTTP 403). No transfer agent, trustee, custodian, auditor, attestor or calculation agent is named on any of them; no reserve is disclosed, because "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way"; and the only third party in the chain disclaims the role - "Republic Core has not independently verified any of the information provided or makes any assurances as to the completeness, accuracy or reliability of any such information provided by RepublicX LLC." NO SOLANA MINT ADDRESS WAS FOUND - Jupiter token-registry searches for rSPAX, rSpaceX, rOpenAI and rANTHROPIC, re-read 2026-09-17, still return only impersonation memecoins, chiefly on the legacy SPL Token program with 1,000,000,000 supplies and pump.fun launchpad tags. The most dangerous of these is 79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x, symbol "rSpaceX", created 2025-06-25T13:12:44Z - the same day as Republic’s announcement - legacy Tokenkeg program, supply 997,884,479.34, 767 holders (768 on 2026-09-16), launchpad-tagged. It is NOT the security, and its holders outnumber the 199 investors in RepublicX’s closed Form D offering by roughly four to one. Also present: GgWZbw7ZkcZQj3Jy6kX1m8HRx7D5YYqcoyGcmnjspump ("SPCX"/"rSpaceX", 2025-06-25), Dc3AjVi3At8YBebo3HPhLXcjR4nc9qRdPJCph9fbRPHp ("rSpaceX", 2025-07-08), AfdbLoS6F6Xa6gbrETZ7Jz6hx3aFjjqrJDjmFrr8UuG7 ("rOpenAI", 2025-06-25), plus a cluster of "preSPAX"/"PreSPAX" Token-2022 mints from April 2026. A genuine restricted Mirror Note mint would plausibly be absent from a DEX aggregator’s index precisely because it cannot trade, so absence from Jupiter is weak evidence of non-existence - but it also means an outside party has no way to find or audit it. Until RepublicX publishes a canonical address, ANY on-chain token bearing a Mirror Token ticker should be treated as an impersonation.

redemption.eligibility: There is no redemption at the holder’s option and no put right. Payment falls due on the EARLIER of a QUALIFYING LIQUIDITY EVENT of the referenced company or a 10-YEAR MATURITY: "Payouts, if any, occur within a reasonable time period (as further described in the offering documentation) after the earlier of the maturity date (i.e., 10 years from the date of issuance) or a Qualified Liquidity Event, plus the expiration of any applicable lock-up period(s)." A Qualified Liquidity Event is defined as "(i) an IPO or other direct listing transaction resulting in SpaceX’s equity interests being listed on a national securities exchange, (ii) a merger or acquisition of its assets or equity interests or (iii) certain other transactions resulting in a public listing or monetization of its equity interests"; dissolution is named alongside IPO and acquisition in the "How it works" steps. If no event occurs, the note still resolves: "On the Maturity Date, Investors will receive the entire value of their repriced securities based on their pro rata share of the increase (or decrease) in the FMV of SpaceX’s common stock." Republic still warns "There is no guarantee of returns, and the timing or likelihood of a liquidity event is not guaranteed", and "No payout of any amount, including your principal investment amount, is guaranteed."
redemption.rails: At maturity or a qualifying liquidity event, "RepublicX pays you based on SpaceX’s share price at that time––the Redemption Price––in proportion to the investment’s Reference Price of $275", and the holder picks the settlement asset: "Each Investor will have the choice of receiving payouts in either (1) U.S. dollars or (2) USDC (U.S. Dollar Coin) to the Investor’s verified Republic Wallet, or such other stablecoin of the Issuer's choosing in the Issuer's sole discretion in the event that USDC is not industry standard at the time payment is due." The payout formula itself is only "described in the Notes and the Offering Documents", which are not public, and no independent calculation agent or dispute mechanism is disclosed. Before then, the only route out is secondary sale: tokens are "locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance", after which "Republic intends to allow secondary trading of Mirror Tokens after a lock-up period on one or more qualifying platforms, including INX Digital" - but "RepublicX retains full discretion whether or not to list any tokens on any qualifying exchange."
redemption.fees: Disclosed in architecture, undisclosed in amount. "All fees reduce your net return. Fees here include a premium built into the Reference Price as well as other fees associated with the Republic platform. In the event secondary trading exists on any qualifying exchange, there may also be fees associated therewith." The premium is inside the $275 Reference Price rather than charged separately - "Republic’s costs are baked into the Reference Price, meaning the bar for making a profit is higher" - and "Investors’ entitlement is reduced/adjusted by fees". No rate, schedule or percentage is published anywhere located; the only hard number in the structure is what the issuer pays its own affiliate: Republic Core receives "an initial onboarding fee of $150,000 and ongoing quarterly fees of $75,000 beginning upon the commencement of the first RX Offering" (Republic Core Form C-AR, p. 47).
redemption.minimum: $50 minimum investment (stated in Republic's press release and confirmed independently by the Form D field minimumInvestmentAccepted = 50); maximum initial purchase stated as $5,000 in the June 2025 release

transferRestrictions.mechanism: UNVERIFIED ON-CHAIN - no mint address was found, so none of the following could be confirmed against Solana mainnet. What is stated, now from the issuer’s own offering page rather than press: (1) a hard 12-month lock - "Mirror Tokens are locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance"; (2) exemption-driven restrictions with a nullity sanction - "There are transfer restrictions based upon the applicable exemption the Notes and any beneficial interests are issued thereunder, including Rule 506 resale limitations, Regulation S distribution-compliance periods and U.S. person restrictions, if applicable. Any transfer in violation of the restrictions is void."; (3) after unlock, transfer only on venues Republic chooses - "on one or more qualifying platforms, including INX Digital", "subject to the applicable rules and limitations on transferability including, without limitation, KYC/AML of the investor", and "RepublicX retains full discretion whether or not to list any tokens on any qualifying exchange"; (4) delivery only into a platform wallet - "To receive Tokens, investors will be required to create a Republic Wallet." IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the "access-control functions, meaning only pre-approved wallets can receive or send tokens, with freeze, clawback, and mint and burn functions" description is Republic’s own but was published for the $NOTE asset; the rSPAX offering pages describe no such token-level powers, so that inference is weaker than the dossier previously recorded, not stronger.

issuers.corporateActions: None flow to the holder, by design - this is a note referencing a company that is not a party to it. No dividend, distribution, voting, proxy, information or inspection right in the referenced company attaches: "You will not receive dividends or other distributions from SpaceX and will have no rights to vote or influence SpaceX’s management and must rely solely on public information, which may be limited, incomplete, or stale." The ONE adjustment question the issuer does address it answers against the holder: "Because the Notes track the value of common shares on a price per share basis, their return may be reduced if SpaceX issues additional shares or equity-linked securities, which could dilute the value of each share" - i.e. dilution risk is borne by the holder with no anti-dilution adjustment. The referenced company’s other corporate actions matter only as inputs to the eventual per-share value, and nothing located explains how a stock split, recapitalisation, down-round, secondary tender, partial acquisition, SPAC merger or reclassification would be treated, nor what happens if a liquidity event is for a different share class than the one referenced. A 10-year maturity does now bound the open-endedness. On the RepublicX side no freeze, clawback, mint or burn power is described on the offering pages at all - that description belongs to Republic’s own $NOTE material.

pricing.notes: There is no reference market. The referenced companies are private, so there is no exchange price, no NBBO and no continuous mark. The ISSUANCE-side price IS disclosed and attributed: "Reference price $275 Based on Yahoo! Finance data as of 9/2/25", against a "Price per security $1.00", with the issuer disclaiming its meaning - "The Reference Price is not, and is not intended to be, a precise fair market value of SpaceX common stock at the time of the offering" - and confirming that its own costs are inside it: "Republic’s costs are baked into the Reference Price, meaning the bar for making a profit is higher." The PAYOUT-side value remains issuer-determined: the Redemption Price is the per-share value at the event or at the 10-year maturity, computed by "the payout formula described in the Notes and the Offering Documents", with no independent calculation agent, no NAV publication, no oracle and no dispute mechanism located. Arbitrage is structurally impossible: no obtainable underlying, no holder-initiated redemption, and no transfers at all for 12 months. Any post-lockup print on a Republic-chosen venue would be a supply-and-demand print inside a permissioned market. The issuer puts the tracking caveat plainly: "The token gives you exposure to SpaceX’s price movements only through the contractual payoff structure, and that exposure is modulated by time, fees, and RepublicX’s credit profile."

venues: None for the first 12 months after issuance — 'Mirror Tokens are locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance'.

Republic Secondary Market and other Republic-chosen venues, post-lockup, permissioned - "Republic intends to allow secondary trading of Mirror Tokens after a lock-up period on one or more qualifying platforms, including INX Digital", and "Republic intends to allow trading of tokens on the Republic Secondary Market with other investors." Note "intends to", and note the discretion: "RepublicX retains full discretion whether or not to list any tokens on any qualifying exchange", with trading "subject to the applicable rules and limitations on transferability including, without limitation, KYC/AML of the investor". Whether any Mirror Note has actually traded anywhere was not verified.
No DEX, AMM, lending market or DeFi integration was found, and none would be expected while transfers are restricted to pre-approved wallets.
NOT a venue: the pump.fun impersonation mints trading under Mirror Token tickers on Solana DEXs (see custodyVerification). Those are unrelated memecoins.

incidents.summary: ASSERTED-BUT-UNFINDABLE OFFERING STATEMENT, found by rwa-sonar after reading the issuer’s own offering page. This supersedes the 2026-09-16 reading of the same facts as a Reg CF/Reg D contradiction: the rSPAX page runs TWO concurrent offerings of the same Contingent Payout Note - "All US Residents" under Regulation Crowdfunding via OpenDeal Portal LLC d/b/a Republic, an SEC-registered funding portal, and "US Accredited & Global Investors" under Rule 506(c) - so the Form D's accredited-only data is the second leg and is not inconsistent with the "open to all" marketing. What IS wrong is a filing: the Reg CF panel tells investors "The Issuer has filed a Form C with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission ... You should review the Form C before investing", and no Form C exists. EDGAR company search returns one CIK for RepublicX (0002080279) whose entire history is Form D and Form D/A; full-text search returns 4 hits for "RepublicX" (those two plus two Republic Core C-ARs), 0 for "rSpaceX" and 0 for "Contingent Payout Note". Reg CF cannot lawfully proceed without a Form C on file, and an investor told to read one cannot find it.

Within hours of Republic's rSpaceX announcement, at least three Solana memecoins appeared using Mirror Token tickers — 'rSpaceX' (79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x, 13:12 UTC, now 768 holders), 'SPCX'/'rSpaceX' (GgWZbw7ZkcZQj3Jy6kX1m8HRx7D5YYqcoyGcmnjspump, 13:32 UTC) and 'rOpenAI' (AfdbLoS6F6Xa6gbrETZ7Jz6hx3aFjjqrJDjmFrr8UuG7, 15:58 UTC) — each a 1-billion-supply launchpad token on the legacy SPL Token program. The impersonation mint has roughly four times as many holders as RepublicX's actual closed offering had investors (199). Not an incident at Republic, but a direct consequence of never publishing a canonical mint address, and the reason a retail investor searching for 'rSpaceX' on Solana will find a memecoin first. Bullish, by contrast, publishes its address and states that 'tokens claiming to represent BLSH from any other contract address are fraudulent'.

openQuestions: IS THERE A MIRROR NOTE TOKEN LIVE ON SOLANA MAINNET AT ALL, AND AT WHAT ADDRESS? Still the central gap, and now confirmed as a disclosure gap rather than a retrieval failure: republic.com/mirror, republic.com/rspax and the Republic Europe campaign page were all read on 2026-09-17 (Wayback) and none of them publishes an address. Republic states the token is "a digital representation of the Notes built on the Solana blockchain, leveraging Republic’s proprietary security token standard"; the Jupiter registry contains only impersonators. A restricted, non-tradable security token would legitimately be absent from a DEX aggregator, so this is not evidence of non-existence - but the tokenization is, from outside, entirely unaudited. NEXT STEP: ask Republic for the canonical address, then read the mint with getAccountInfo.

RESOLVED as a two-track offering, with one filing still missing. Reg CF and Reg D are not alternative accounts of one offering: the rSPAX page runs an "All US Residents" Reg CF offering via OpenDeal Portal LLC d/b/a Republic, an SEC-registered funding portal, alongside a "US Accredited & Global Investors" Rule 506(c) offering, both of the same Contingent Payout Note. The Form D on EDGAR is the 506(c) leg. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: the Reg CF panel asserts "The Issuer has filed a Form C with the ... SEC", and no Form C is on EDGAR - one CIK for RepublicX (0002080279), history D and D/A only; full-text search returns 0 hits for "rSpaceX" and 0 for "Contingent Payout Note". Was a Form C filed under another filer, withdrawn, or never filed?

ANSWERED: RepublicX holds nothing against the notes, and the obligation is funded by the issuer’s business plus a parent keepwell. "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset"; repayment comes "from funds available to RepublicX from its business and operations and not from any dedicated pool of investor proceeds"; and the sole credit support is "that certain keepwell agreement of OpenDeal Inc., as discussed in the Offering Documents". WHAT REMAINS OPEN: the keepwell is not published - its cap, triggers, term and enforceability by noteholders are all unread, and it is now the single most important unread document in this dossier.

HOW IS THE PAYOUT CALCULATED, AND BY WHOM? Partly answered: the payout is the per-share value of SpaceX common stock at a Qualified Liquidity Event or at the 10-year maturity, "in proportion to the investment’s Reference Price of $275", with Republic’s costs inside that Reference Price. But the formula itself is only "described in the Notes and the Offering Documents", and no independent calculation agent, adjustment provision or dispute mechanism is disclosed. Obtain the Note and the subscription agreement.

ANSWERED: a Qualified Liquidity Event is "(i) an IPO or other direct listing transaction resulting in SpaceX’s equity interests being listed on a national securities exchange, (ii) a merger or acquisition of its assets or equity interests or (iii) certain other transactions resulting in a public listing or monetization of its equity interests", with dissolution named alongside IPO and acquisition in the "How it works" steps; and if none occurs the note matures at 10 years, when "Investors will receive the entire value of their repriced securities based on their pro rata share of the increase (or decrease) in the FMV of SpaceX’s common stock". Still unread: whether a tender offer, secondary round or partial acquisition qualifies, which is inside the Note’s own definition.

IS THE POST-LOCKUP SECONDARY MARKET ACTUALLY LIVE? Republic "intends to allow secondary trading of Mirror Tokens after a lock-up period on one or more qualifying platforms, including INX Digital", and "RepublicX retains full discretion whether or not to list any tokens on any qualifying exchange". rSpaceX notes issued in June 2025 unlocked around June 2026; those in the Form D offering (first sale 2025-11-28) unlock around November 2026. Whether any Mirror Note has ever actually traded, where, at what price and under whose regulatory permission is unverified - and it is the test of whether this is a tokenized security or a database entry.

WHICH ENTITY AND WHICH REGIME APPLIES TO EUROPEAN HOLDERS? Partly answered: the campaign page states the issuer is still RepublicX LLC ("An unsecured debt security issued by RepublicX LLC", location Delaware, United States) and that the promoter is Seedrs Limited t/a Republic Europe, FCA FRN 550317, which approved the campaign as a financial promotion on 2025-09-17 and "will act as Custodian rather than provide our standard nominee service". Still open: whether the note terms, lock-up and payout are identical to the US legs, and whether the same Solana token is used. Note the size asymmetry - the UK/EU channel raised £849,170 from 850 investors against the US 506(c) leg’s $585,205 from 199.

HOW MANY MIRROR NOTE SERIES EXIST AND WHAT IS OUTSTANDING? Republic’s grid names 24 reference companies with statuses (SpaceX live; Perplexity, Anthropic and Epic Games "Filled"; the rest reservations). Only ONE offering appears on EDGAR ($3.5M offered, $585,205 sold, closed). Are the other series unfiled, filed elsewhere, offered only outside the US, or not yet launched? Is each series a separate token, and does each have its own claim on RepublicX or do they share one balance sheet? Note the answer matters more now that proceeds are known to be unsegregated and spent on general corporate purposes.

WHO ARE THE 767 HOLDERS OF THE IMPERSONATION MINT, AND DOES REPUBLIC KNOW? 79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x ("rSpaceX", created within hours of the announcement) still had 767 holders on 2026-09-17, roughly four times the 199 investors in RepublicX’s actual offering. No Republic warning about impersonation mints was located on any of the three pages now read. Publishing canonical addresses would cost nothing and remains the single highest-value disclosure improvement available to this issuer.

DOES THE TOKEN STANDARD REALLY CARRY FREEZE AND CLAWBACK FOR THE MIRROR NOTES? Now less likely than the dossier assumed, not more: the "access-control ... freeze, clawback, and mint and burn" description is Republic’s own but was published for the $NOTE asset, and neither the rSPAX offering page nor the /mirror page - both read in full on 2026-09-17 - describes any token-level power over holders’ balances. What they describe is contractual restriction ("Any transfer in violation of the restrictions is void") and listing discretion. Without a mint address nothing can be confirmed, which is why forcedTransfers and reflectLegalDecisions stay "unknown".

METHODOLOGICAL NOTE FOR THE MAINTAINER: confidence was raised from "low" to "medium" on 2026-09-17 because the reason for "low" no longer holds - the issuer’s own primary pages have now been read. They were still HTTP 403 (Cloudflare, consistent with a geographic block) to curl with a browser UA and to WebFetch, but the Internet Archive was up, so republic.com/mirror, republic.com/rspax and europe.republic.com/rspax-mirror-notes were read from Wayback snapshots dated 2025-10-12, 2025-09-16 and 2025-10-07. The SEC filings, the Republic Core Form C-AR and the Solana registry reads are first-hand and current.

Solana mainnet / registry reads by rwa-sonar on 2026-09-16: Jupiter token-registry searches for rSPAX, rSpaceX, rOPENAI, rANTHROPIC and 'Mirror' returned no genuine RepublicX instrument, only legacy-SPL and Token-2022 launchpad memecoins. keyGovernance.evidence: No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release or accessible page, and none was located in the token registries, so no authority key could be read from the chain (stocks/findings.md, Republic Mirror entry). Republic describes its own standard as carrying freeze, clawback, mint and burn functions, but nothing ties those powers to an identified key.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Nothing states or implies that the chain is the legal record, and the structure argues against it. This is an unsecured note of a private Delaware LLC: the obligation exists under the note agreement and the holder's entitlement is recorded on RepublicX's own books. There is no transfer agent, no registrar and no register of any kind disclosed; transfers are locked for 12 months and then permitted only inside Republic's own permissioned secondary market; and the token standard is described as giving RepublicX freeze, clawback, mint and burn powers over holders' balances. A ledger the issuer can rewrite at will, gating a claim documented off-chain, is a convenience layer. Note also the asymmetry with the equity cases: for a registered share there is at least a contest between a transfer agent's register and the chain. Here there is no competing register to point to — which means the on-chain balance is not authoritative and nothing else is published either.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: The most restricted of the three issuers examined, on three independent grounds. (1) An absolute 12-month prohibition: 'Mirror Tokens are locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance' — this follows from the Securities Act resale restrictions attaching to both Reg CF and Rule 506(c) securities, so it holds whichever exemption actually applied. (2) After unlock, transfer is not free but confined to Republic's own permissioned venue: 'Republic intends to allow trading of tokens on the Republic Secondary Market with other investors' — note 'intends to', and note that whether the venue is live for Mirror Notes is unverified. (3) Token-level access control: Republic's Solana security-token standard is described as having 'access-control functions, meaning only pre-approved wallets can receive or send tokens'. Caveat on the evidence: none of this could be verified on-chain because no mint address was found, and the access-control description was given for Republic's $NOTE asset and inferred to the Mirror Tokens.

bearerRedemption.reason: There is no redemption at all, let alone bearer redemption. No put right and no holder-initiated exit exists. Payment happens only if and when a qualifying liquidity event occurs at the referenced private company — 'When a qualifying liquidity event occurs, RepublicX will distribute the fair value of common shares of the company' — and Republic itself warns 'There is no guarantee that the company will ever conduct an IPO' and that 'the timing or likelihood of a liquidity event is not guaranteed'. Presenting the token to any third party gets nothing: no third party has any obligation under it, least of all the referenced company, which 'has not reviewed, endorsed, or participated in this offering in any capacity'.

forcedTransfers.reason: Claimed elsewhere, absent here, and unverifiable either way. Republic describes its Solana security-token standard as including "freeze, clawback, and mint and burn functions to ensure legally compliant trading", which would supply the mechanism for court-ordered seizure, theft recovery, loss recovery and inheritance. Three problems prevent scoring it "yes", one of them new. First, that description was published for Republic’s own $NOTE asset rather than for the Mirror Notes. Second, and new as of 2026-09-17: the rSPAX offering page and the /mirror page were both read in full and neither describes any freeze, clawback, burn or forced-transfer power over the tokens - what they describe is contractual, exemption-driven transfer restriction ("Any transfer in violation of the restrictions is void") and listing discretion. So the inference is weaker than before, not stronger. Third and decisively, no mint address was located, so nothing could be checked against Solana mainnet - unlike Bullish and Securitize, where the permanent delegate and freeze authority were read directly off the mint. Recorded as unknown on the principle that an unverified capability is not a capability, and note that even if present the powers would sit with a single private LLC with no named role, no disclosed policy and no regulated registrar.

titleDeed.reason: Emphatically not, and the issuer says so. The token conveys no ownership of the referenced company: it 'offers economic exposure to SpaceX through blockchain without giving equity or ownership rights' and 'does not represent actual ownership or equity in SpaceX'. What the holder has is a derived, contingent, unsecured contractual claim against RepublicX LLC — a debt note whose payout references a third party's share value. Nor is it a title to anything RepublicX holds, since the note is unsecured and no backing asset is even disclosed. This is the cleanest 'no' in the set and the structural difference from the Bullish and Securitize dossiers, where the token IS the registered share.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Not established, but the evidence is now two-sided rather than absent. The offering page requires a platform wallet - "To receive Tokens, investors will be required to create a Republic Wallet", "Yes, a Republic Wallet is required in order to participate in these offerings and to receive Tokens" - and pays out "to the Investor’s verified Republic Wallet". The /mirror marketing page claims the opposite emphasis: "Investments custodied in your own wallets, trackable on blockchain, backed by Republic." Nothing states whether a Republic Wallet is self-custodial or hosted, and the UK/EU channel is plainly not self-custody at all: "If you invest in this Campaign, Seedrs will act as Custodian rather than provide our standard nominee service." With no mint address the distribution of holdings across accounts cannot be inspected either. Left unknown rather than guessed.

issuerIndependent.reason: Total dependence on a single counterparty, and more so than in any other structure examined. RepublicX LLC is a Delaware LLC formed in 2025 with no disclosed capital, no transfer agent, no trustee, no collateral and no independent calculation agent. If it disappears the token means nothing: the payout is its unsecured promise, the 'fair value' determination is its own, the secondary market is its affiliate's, and the token's transferability depends on its access-control keys. The Form D shows an entity that raised $585,205 and closed the offering early ('We do not intend to sell the remaining'), against notes whose eventual payout could be many multiples of subscription value if the referenced company appreciates — with nothing located to indicate how that obligation would be funded. Compare the equity cases: there, the SHARE survives the platform's failure even when the TOKEN does not. Here, nothing survives.

presetJurisdiction.reason: The applicable legal framework is identifiable even though the instrument's own terms were not readable: a Delaware LLC with New York offices, a US federal securities exemption claimed on the public record (Form D, Rule 506(c), file no. 021-565769), a named manager (OpenDeal Inc.) and a named signatory (Jeffrey Vier), with a separate and clearly demarcated UK/EU channel through Republic Europe. A US holder would know which courts and which regulator to approach. Marked 'yes' on that basis, but with two real qualifications: the governing-law clause of the note itself is unread because the offering pages are geo-blocked; and the regulatory characterisation is internally contradicted — marketed as Reg CF, filed as Reg D 506(c) — so which exemption governs the securities-law treatment of any given holder's notes is genuinely unclear.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent exists anywhere in the structure, and this is the most complete absence in the set. No transfer agent, no trustee, no custodian, no auditor report on the notes, no proof-of-reserve, no NAV or valuation publication, no independent calculation agent, no smart-contract audit, no published mint address and no on-chain metadata to attach anything to. Every fact about the instrument — its backing, its value, its outstanding amount, its holder list — is RepublicX's unverified assertion. The referenced companies explicitly disclaim involvement, which removes the one party who could authenticate the economic reference.

aiReady.reason: Fails on every limb. Transfers are prohibited outright for 12 months, then restricted to a permissioned affiliate venue among vetted investors; the token standard is described as permitting only pre-approved wallets to send or receive; and subscription runs through a retail investment platform's KYC/AML onboarding with per-investor purchase caps ($5,000 initial), which is exactly the kind of identity and suitability gate an autonomous agent cannot pass. Fails on unconditionalTransfers regardless.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: Cannot be established. The mechanism may exist — Republic's token standard is described as including freeze and clawback — but it is unverified on-chain and only inferred to apply to the Mirror Notes, and no contractual undertaking to honour judicial or regulatory orders was readable, because the note agreement and offering pages could not be retrieved. There is also no regulated intermediary in the structure carrying such obligations by operation of law: no transfer agent means no Exchange Act §17A duties, no Rule 17Ad-17 lost-holder obligations and no escheat process. Note the countervailing point that keeps this from being a 'no': a plain unsecured note of a Delaware LLC is an ordinary contractual claim that US courts can adjudicate and garnish by conventional means — the legal system can reach the CLAIM even if nobody can demonstrate it can reach the TOKEN.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Buyer-and-seller agreement is worth nothing here for a full year, and little after. For 12 months no transfer is permitted on any terms. Afterwards, Republic 'intends to allow' trading on its own secondary market among vetted investors, with pre-approved wallets on the token side — so the counterparty set, the venue and the permission all sit with the issuer's group, not with the parties. Two willing counterparties cannot effect a valid transfer of a Mirror Note by agreeing to one.

attestations.statement: The issuer states plainly that holders get no equity and no ownership: "If you invest, you’re buying a debt instrument offered by RepublicX and represented by the rSPAX Tokens. You have no right whatsoever to equity in SpaceX, RepublicX, or Republic by virtue of investing in any offering", and "Investors’ respective creditor rights do not consist of any shareholders’ rights". Reinforced by an unusually thorough eight-limb affiliation disclaimer: "SpaceX has not reviewed, approved, authorized, endorsed, sponsored, or consented to any aspect of this security, token, marketing material, or transaction structure."

"Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset" (republic.com/rspax, FAQ "Am I investing in a fund?").

findings.statement: No custodian, trustee or collateral agent is named anywhere, and the reason is now on the record rather than inferred: there is nothing to custody. "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset", and the notes are repaid "from funds available to RepublicX from its business and operations and not from any dedicated pool of investor proceeds". So "mirror" is a payout formula, not a backed position. The only custodian anywhere in the structure is on the UK/EU channel, where Seedrs Limited "will act as Custodian rather than provide our standard nominee service" for the investment position itself.
findings.quote: Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset.
findings.quoteNote: Evidence moved from the press republication to the issuer’s own offering page, read from Wayback snapshot 20250916201851. This answers what the finding called the single largest unknown.

findings.statement: The sole determinant of what a holder receives is RepublicX's own determination of 'the fair value of common shares of the company' at a qualifying liquidity event, in USD or USDC. No independent calculation agent, no valuation methodology, no adjustment provisions for splits or multi-class events, no fallback if no event occurs, no maturity date and no dispute mechanism. The party that owes the money decides how much is owed.
findings.quote: What is the Reference Price and how is it determined? The Reference Price for this rSPAX offering is $275.The Reference Price functions, in part, as the basis for how much an investor gets paid, if at all, at the 10 year maturity or at a qualifying event for SpaceX
findings.quoteNote: The missing space after "$275." is as printed. The issuance-side price is disclosed and attributed to Yahoo! Finance as of 9/2/25; the payout-side formula is still only "described in the Notes and the Offering Documents".

findings.statement: No NAV, mark, indicative value or valuation methodology is published at any cadence. For a structured note this is the product, and it is unreadable.
findings.quote: The Reference Price is not, and is not intended to be, a precise fair market value of SpaceX common stock at the time of the offering.
findings.quoteNote: No NAV, mark or indicative value is published at any cadence, and the issuer disclaims that its one published price is a fair value.

findings.statement: The referenced companies are private, so there is no market price to feed and no oracle was located. This is the structural reason the "mirror" is an intention rather than an enforced tracking mechanism.
findings.quote: must rely solely on public information, which may be limited, incomplete, or stale
findings.quoteNote: From the FAQ "If I invest, am I now an owner of SpaceX?". The issuer confirms there is no feed to rely on, only public information about a private company.

findings.statement: Investors subscribe through the Republic platform with per-investor caps, which entails identity verification, and the filed Rule 506(c) exemption requires reasonable steps to verify accredited status. But no KYC policy, provider, sanctions-screening commitment or accreditation-verification method was published, and the accredited-verification requirement sits oddly with marketing aimed at everyday investors.
findings.quote: Republic intends to make tokens available for secondary trading after the conclusion of any applicable lock-up periods, subject to the applicable rules and limitations on transferability including, without limitation, KYC/AML of the investor.
findings.quoteNote: KYC/AML is named as a transfer condition, but no policy, provider, sanctions-screening commitment or accredited-verification method is published, and Rule 506(c) requires reasonable steps to verify accredited status.

findings.statement: Republic describes its Solana security-token standard as carrying 'freeze, clawback, and mint and burn functions to ensure legally compliant trading', but no mint address was located, so the authority public keys are unknown and no role, officer, escalation path or key-management arrangement is disclosed. If present, the powers sit with a single unregulated private LLC.
findings.quoteNote: NOTHING TO QUOTE, and the position is now weaker rather than stronger: the freeze/clawback description belongs to Republic’s $NOTE material, and neither republic.com/rspax nor republic.com/mirror - both read in full on 2026-09-17 - describes any token-level power over holders’ balances. Evidence stays stocks/findings.md.

findings.statement: Republic maintains public product and offering pages carrying substantive terms, and they are unreachable from outside the US: republic.com/mirror, republic.com/rspax and europe.republic.com/rspax-mirror-notes returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to curl with a browser user agent and to WebFetch on both 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-17. On 2026-09-17 the Internet Archive was up, so all three were read from Wayback snapshots (20251012164756, 20250916201851, 20251007111149). The limitation is therefore geographic availability and staleness, not absence: a reader outside the US cannot read the live terms of a security they hold, and the newest snapshot available was about eleven months old.
findings.quote: Mirror Tokens are digital assets issued by RepublicX LLC that are designed to mirror the economic outcome of investing in a specific private company (“target company”) — giving you the chance to participate in the potential economic upside of the companies, without making a direct investment.

keyGovernance.evidence: No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release or accessible page, and none was located in the token registries, so no authority key could be read from the chain (stocks/findings.md, Republic Mirror entry). Republic describes its own standard as carrying freeze, clawback, mint and burn functions, but nothing ties those powers to an identified key.

issuers.name: Securitize SECZ
issuers.issuerText: Securitize Corp. (NYSE: SECZ) — the securities issuer is the listed company itself (Delaware corporation, SEC CIK 0002094496), which is also its own tokenization platform, its own SEC-registered transfer agent (Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC) and the operator of the broker-dealer/ATS that gates access. This vertical integration is the defining feature of the structure: there is no independent transfer agent anywhere in the stack, unlike Superstate (where an independent Recordkeeping Transfer Agent holds the master file) or Bullish (where Equiniti is still a third party until Q1 2027).
chains: Avalanche (larger deployment per the S-1; contract not verified here)

products: Tokenized SECZ — 'a natively tokenized version of our common stock', enabled on the Closing Date of the business combination (2026-07-01) and live from the NYSE listing (2026-07-02), issued on Solana and Avalanche. 'Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class.'
