issuers.entityJurisdiction: Delaware corporation, principal operations United States. All regulated entities in the stack are SEC-registered/FINRA-member US entities.
issuers.governingLaw: Delaware General Corporation Law governs the common stock and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing, the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21) and the broker-dealer/ATS gating access. No separate token terms of service or holder agreement for Tokenized SECZ was located; the operative public instrument is the Form S-1 prospectus risk factor plus the Securitize platform's general investor terms (not located in tokenized-SECZ-specific form).
issuers.regulatoryStatus: The most heavily regulated of the three Solana-native issuers examined, and the only one where the tokenization vendor is itself the registrant. The underlying security is registered common stock of a Delaware SEC-reporting company listed on the NYSE (S-4 registration statement effective 2026-06-05; S-1 filed 2026-07-31, EFFECT 2026-08-07; 424B3 prospectuses 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-13). Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638). The S-1 describes the group as 'the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration'. Access to the tokenized form is intermediated by a regulated broker-dealer: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer' (note: the S-1 renders the entity name as 'Securities Markets, LLC'. RESOLVED 2026-09-17 against a primary source: Securitize's own 2026-07-02 press release names 'Securitize Markets, LLC, an SEC-registered broker-dealer and member FINRA/SIPC that operates an SEC-regulated Alternative Trading System (ATS)', so the S-1 wording is a typographical error in a registration statement and the gatekeeping broker-dealer is Securitize Markets, LLC). No exemptive relief or no-action letter for the tokenized form was located; the S-1 warns that 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations'.
issuers.holderClaim: The holder owns the actual registered common share. The S-1 risk factor is unambiguous on two points at once: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class' and 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'. The issuer's own press release adds that this is an 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE' and that 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Holders may move between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. There is no SPV, receipt or nominee layer in the legal structure — but access runs through a broker-dealer's onboarding, so whether the holder is a registered holder of record in their own name or a customer of the broker-dealer is NOT established by any document located, and this is the central unresolved question for this issuer.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: No custodian is interposed for the security itself — the token is the share and the register is Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC's master securityholder file. For its own corporate digital assets Securitize discloses self-custody via Fireblocks MPC ('enables us to retain exclusive control over the authorization of transactions without ever generating or storing a traditional private key'), and states that 'In the case of Securitize-issued tokenized securities held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure, Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Investor-side custody may be self-custody (see transferRestrictions) or broker/custodian-held; the split is not disclosed.

custodyVerification.agent: Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC (SEC-registered transfer agent, File No. 084-06638, CIK 0001782266) — an affiliate of the issuer, not an independent party
custodyVerification.frequency: continuous, claimed — 'every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time'; multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file to ensure that total outstanding units remain consistent and singular across chains'
custodyVerification.notes: NO PUBLIC VERIFICATION FEED. Securitize publishes no instruments API, no per-token supply endpoint, no allowlist enumeration and no reconciliation report for SECZ. The token's TokenMetadata URI (https://metadata.securitize.io/secz.json) resolves but contains only name, symbol, description and image — no CUSIP/ISIN, no register link, no supply, no attestation. The Securitize Connect API (https://sec-connect-api-docs.securitize.io/wallets) documents the whitelisting mechanism but is an authenticated partner API, not a public verification surface. VERIFIED ON SOLANA MAINNET BY RWA-SONAR, 2026-09-16 (slot ~447535518): mint 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED is a Token-2022 mint, decimals 6, supply 148,998.000000, name 'Securitize Corp.', symbol 'SECZ'; 117 Token-2022 accounts exist for the mint (getProgramAccounts with mint filter); extensions MetadataPointer, PausableConfig, DefaultAccountState=Frozen, PermanentDelegate, ScaledUiAmount, TokenMetadata; NO TransferHook. Authority topology, and this is the notable finding: mintAuthority == freezeAuthority == 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs, and getAccountInfo on that address returns null — a zero-lamport, never-initialized account, which is the signature of a program-derived address used as a CPI signer rather than a funded wallet. That is a MEANINGFULLY BETTER key posture than Bullish, whose mint/freeze authority is a plain funded wallet: it implies a Securitize program mediates minting and thawing. It is not proof — the owning program was not identified, and the separate authority on the extensions (D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS, which holds permanentDelegate, pausable, scaledUiAmount, metadataPointer and tokenMetadata update authority) was not resolved either. MEASURED CONTRADICTION: press coverage (CoinDesk, PRNewswire, RWA.xyz-sourced) reports '$295 million in tokenized shares'. The Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens, worth roughly $1.24M at the ~$8.35 price Jupiter reported on 2026-09-16 — about 0.4% of $295M. Either essentially all of the $295M sits on Avalanche (consistent with the S-1, which puts the locked-up business-combination shares there) or the $295M figure is not comparable to on-chain supply. Any grading that attributes the $295M headline to Solana is wrong by more than two orders of magnitude.

redemption.eligibility: Holders who have completed the broker-dealer onboarding: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The issuer's press release adds that the tokenized form is for 'eligible U.S. investors' subject to 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. Certain Avalanche holdings are additionally subject to business-combination lock-up agreements.
redemption.rails: Bidirectional switching between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. No burn address, no processing time, no fee schedule and no step-by-step process was located in any public document. Because the transfer agent and the platform are the same group, the switch is an internal book movement rather than a coordination between two agents — mechanically simpler than the Superstate peer's DRS route, but also entirely un-auditable from outside.

transferRestrictions.mechanism: program-mediated, per-token whitelist. On-chain: Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so every new SECZ token account is frozen at birth and only the freeze authority (8Twerer..., an apparent program PDA) can thaw it; plus PausableConfig for a global halt. Off-chain: the Securitize Connect API documents wallet whitelisting scoped to a specific token ('adds a wallet address to the whitelist of an specific token', requiring a tokenId, since 'in a given domain there may be multiple tokens'), with wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and a 'not-authorised' response state. Notably the whitelist is NOT tied to a platform-hosted wallet: 'This is not required, as the whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' — a self-custodied address can be whitelisted directly. Contractually: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche holdings carry business-combination lock-ups. US persons are the TARGET market here ('eligible U.S. investors'), which inverts the usual tokenized-equity geofence.

issuers.corporateActions: Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. Emergency halt: PausableConfig on the mint, with no published policy for its use.

pricing.notes: The same class trades on NYSE under SECZ, so a continuous reference price exists, and the token has on-chain liquidity: 'Trading of Tokenized SECZ on Solana is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners', and Jupiter priced the mint at ~$8.35 on 2026-09-16 with a reported holder count of 44 and roughly $1.24M market value. The issuer is candid about the basis risk in its own prospectus: 'the simultaneous existence of both could potentially fragment liquidity across platforms, affect bid-ask spreads (particularly outside NYSE trading hours), and result in price discrepancies between Tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ—especially if arbitrage is limited by operational or regulatory constraints', and 'Blockchain-based trading mechanisms may have significantly less liquidity and volume compared to national securities exchanges, such as NYSE'. Arbitrage is real but constrained twice over: the switch between forms has no published latency, and only broker-dealer-onboarded persons can hold the tokenized side at all, so the arbitrageur set is permissioned. Jupiter reported a -100% 24h volume change on 2026-09-16, i.e. no trades that day — the on-chain market exists but is thin. No oracle price feed for the Solana mint was located.

venues: On-chain liquidity on Solana via unnamed 'on-chain liquidity provision partners' (S-1). Jupiter indexes and prices the mint (isVerified true, tags token-2022/verified), so DEX routing exists — a materially more open venue posture than Bullish, where 'AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled'.
Securitize's own SEC-registered broker-dealer and alternative trading system, 'approved for digital asset securities primary and secondary market trading'.
NYSE — for the non-tokenized common stock.
Avalanche — the larger tokenized deployment; venue arrangements there not examined.
Reported 2026-08-20 but unverified by rwa-sonar: SECZ linked to Solana on-chain credit markets (collateral use).

incidents.summary: Observation by rwa-sonar, not an announced incident: the widely-cited '$295 million of tokenized SECZ' does not correspond to the Solana deployment. The Solana Token-2022 mint held 148,998 tokens on 2026-09-16 (~$1.24M at ~$8.35), i.e. roughly 0.4% of the headline figure, across 117 token accounts. The S-1 places the locked-up business-combination shares on Avalanche, which is the likely home of the balance. The headline figure appears to be a cross-chain (or Avalanche-dominated) total that press coverage attached to the Solana launch; nothing published by the issuer breaks it down per chain. A grader reading '$295M on Solana' would be off by more than two orders of magnitude.

Re-measured 2026-09-17: the Solana mint holds 148,998.000000 tokens across 116 Token-2022 accounts (slot 447827107), against 163,265,685 shares outstanding at 2026-07-01, i.e. about 0.09% of the class. Nothing published breaks the $295M headline down per chain.

incidents.summary: Discrepancy inside the issuer's own prospectus, worth recording as the marketing-versus-instrument split this project exists to arbitrate. The S-1 business section says Securitize 'issues, manages, and records securities natively on-chain — meaning that instead of relying on disconnected systems across brokers, custodians, and clearinghouses, every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time'. The same document's risk factors say multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file', that in a fork 'Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record', and that Securitize keeps 'manual safeguards ... which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent'. The risk factors describe an off-chain control book with the chain as its projection; the business section describes the chain as the ledger. The risk factors are the operative description.

The risk-factor half is on p. 31 (control book and master securityholder file, issuer decides the authoritative chain on a fork) and p. 20 (manual safeguards should the automated blockchain systems fail). Both halves re-read verbatim 2026-09-17.

Nothing found. On-chain, pausableConfig.paused was still false at slot 447827107, so no pause has been left in effect.

documents.title: Securitize Corp. Form S-1, filed 2026-07-31 — THE definitive primary document. Contains the 'tokenization of our common stock' risk factor ('Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class'; broker-dealer onboarding gate; Solana trading via liquidity partners; Avalanche lock-ups; price-discrepancy warning), the blockchain-fork risk factor (control book, master securityholder file, Securitize determines the authoritative chain), the Fireblocks/manual-safeguards disclosure, and the 21-chain integration list.
Securitize Corp. Form 424B3 prospectus, filed 2026-08-07 (registration effective per EFFECT 2026-08-07)
Securitize Corp. Form 8-K filed 2026-07-08 — the business-combination 'super 8-K' (Items 1.01, 2.01, 3.01, 3.02, 3.03, 4.01, 5.01, 5.02, 5.03, 5.05, 9.01) for the Closing on 2026-07-01
Securitize Corp. Form 8-K filed 2026-08-12 with Exhibit 99.1, Q2 2026 earnings release (mentions Solana)
Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC SEC transfer-agent registration filings, SEC File No. 084-06638, CIK 0001782266 (TA-1 plus multiple TA-1/A amendments and annual TA-2 reports)

Securitize press release, 2026-07-02 — 'Tokenizing SECZ: Securitize Brings Its Own Public Stock Onchain at Listing Day'. Names Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC; 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE'; 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.'

Securitize Connect API documentation — Wallets. Documents per-token whitelisting (tokenId required), wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and 'not-authorised', and that 'whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' (i.e. self-custodied addresses can be whitelisted).

SECZ token metadata document referenced by the mint's TokenMetadata extension — resolves, on an issuer-controlled domain, but carries only name, symbol, description and image; no CUSIP/ISIN, no register link, no supply, no attestation

NOT FOUND: no token terms of service or holder agreement specific to Tokenized SECZ; no published Solana or Avalanche contract addresses in any issuer filing or release; no smart-contract audit for the Solana deployment; no reconciliation report or proof-of-register; no public supply/holder API.

openQuestions: MINT ATTRIBUTION IS INFERRED, NOT PUBLISHED. Securitize has published no Solana contract address anywhere located. 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED is attributed on the strength of its TokenMetadata URI pointing at metadata.securitize.io, matching name/symbol, the Token-2022 compliance extension set, a 2026-06-29 creation date (three days before listing) and a registry verified flag. That is strong circumstantial evidence, not issuer confirmation. Given four SECZ-branded impersonation mints on Solana, the single highest-value next step is asking Securitize IR to publish canonical addresses. Treat the address as high-confidence-but-unconfirmed until then.

Where is the $295M? Press reports $295M of tokenized SECZ; the Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens (~$1.24M). The S-1 puts locked-up business-combination shares on Avalanche, so the balance is presumably there — but Securitize publishes no per-chain supply figures and nothing reconciles the headline to the chains. The Avalanche contract address should be identified and its supply read to close this.

Is a tokenized holder a holder of record in their own name, or a customer position behind the group's broker-dealer? This is the most consequential unanswered question for grading, and it determines whether titleDeed really behaves like the Superstate peer's (where the holder's name, address and TIN sit on the register). Access runs through 'the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer', which is the shape of a customer relationship — yet the whitelisting API explicitly supports addresses with no Securitize iD profile, which is the shape of direct registration. Both cannot be the general case.

What is the correct name of the gatekeeping broker-dealer? The S-1 says 'Securities Markets, LLC'; Securitize's broker-dealer is publicly known as Securitize Markets, LLC. Most likely a typo in a registration statement, but it is the entity that controls who may hold the security, and it should be confirmed against the FINRA/SEC BD registration rather than assumed.

Which entity holds the on-chain authorities, and under what program? 8Twerer... (mint + freeze) is an apparent PDA whose owning program was not identified; D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA... (permanent delegate, pause, split, metadata) was not resolved at all. Whether these sit with Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC (the regulated registrar) or with an operating affiliate matters legally, and whether the program has a timelock or multisig gate matters for grading. Fireblocks MPC is disclosed for corporate treasury only.

What are the 117 token accounts? 148,998 tokens across 117 accounts, with Jupiter reporting 44 holders and a top-holders concentration of ~11.7%. How many are investor self-custody wallets versus platform/custodian/liquidity-pool accounts is unknown. getTokenLargestAccounts on the public RPC returned HTTP 429 on 2026-09-16 and should be retried against a paid endpoint.

Who are the 'on-chain liquidity provision partners' on Solana? The S-1 says Solana trading 'is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners' without naming them. Since holding SECZ requires whitelisting, a liquidity pool must itself be whitelisted — so the pool addresses, and whether pool LPs must be onboarded, are open. Jupiter reported zero volume in the 24h to 2026-09-16.

Is SECZ actually live as DeFi collateral? Press of 2026-08-20 reports SECZ linked to Solana on-chain credit markets. Unverified by rwa-sonar. If true it would need an oracle feed (none located) and would raise the same jurisdiction-of-use question the Superstate/Kamino integration raises.

Has the fork policy ever been applied, and who bears the loss? The S-1's fork provisions are the most developed chain-exception policy in this universe, but they allocate authority without allocating loss: nothing states what happens to a holder whose tokens end up on the chain Securitize does not recognise, or who compensates them. Also note the dependency it creates — the tie-break heuristic is whichever fork 'principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' recognise.

How do dividends, proxy voting and splits work for a tokenized holder? Securitize sells 'distributions, dividend issuances' as transfer-agent services and runs them for third-party issuers, but Securitize Corp. pays no dividend, the ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, and no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented. Untested on its own stock. Note the earnout structure (VWAP thresholds of $15/$20/$25 triggering Securitize Earnout Shares over five years from Closing) will cause share issuance that must propagate to the mint — a live, dated test of the control-book-to-chain path.
What is the token-to-nontokenized switch latency and fee? Unpublished, and it is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies.

Has the Solana token program been independently audited? Nothing public ties an audit to this deployment, despite Securitize's scale (BUIDL alone was >60% of its tokenized AUM at 2025-09-30) and its 21-chain integration.
sources: Solana mainnet JSON-RPC reads by rwa-sonar on 2026-09-16 (slots 447535518-447535519): getAccountInfo (jsonParsed) on mint 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED for Token-2022 extensions, authorities and supply; getTokenSupply (148,998.000000); getAccountInfo on 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs (returned null — zero-lamport uninitialized address); getProgramAccounts on Token-2022 filtered to the mint (117 accounts). getTokenLargestAccounts returned HTTP 429 and remains unread. The Avalanche deployment was not examined.

keyGovernance.evidence: RPC getAccountInfo, 2026-09-16 (stocks/findings.md, Securitize entry): the mint and freeze authority 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs returns null - zero lamports, never initialized - which is the shape of a PDA used as a CPI signer, so minting and thawing are program-mediated. The owning program was not identified and its upgrade authority is unknown. RESOLVED 2026-09-17: the permanent-delegate/pause/split/metadata authority D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS is NOT a PDA - getAccountInfo returns an initialized, funded, system-program-owned account with zero data (499,971,639 lamports = 0.49997 SOL, owner 11111111111111111111111111111111, executable false), which is a plain keypair wallet with no multisig account behind it. So claw-back, global pause and the split multiplier sit behind one ordinary private key even though minting and thawing are program-mediated. Which entity holds it is still unattributed.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Securitize's own prospectus decides this three times over, against its own marketing. (1) The control book: multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file to ensure that total outstanding units remain consistent and singular across chains' — a master securityholder file that reconciles the chains is by definition above them. (2) The fork policy: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities.' If the issuer picks which ledger is authoritative, the ledger is not authoritative. (3) The manual fallback: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Against this, the business section claims 'every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time', and third-party commentary claims 'a transfer of a SECZ token on Solana or Avalanche constitutes a transfer of the underlying security in the official company records'. The latter may well describe the operational reality — the transfer agent and the chain operator are the same firm, so the propagation is immediate and there is no inter-party reconciliation gap, which is the strongest version of this architecture anyone is running. It is still a control book with an on-chain projection.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Gated at both layers. On-chain: the mint carries DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so any account opened by a non-whitelisted wallet is frozen at birth and cannot receive; only the freeze authority (8Twerer...) can thaw it; and PausableConfig allows a global halt. Off-chain: whitelisting is per-token through the Securitize Connect API, and 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The press release: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Specific Avalanche positions carry business-combination lock-ups on top. The one point in Securitize's favour: there IS on-chain liquidity ('trading ... enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners', Jupiter-routable), so whitelisted-to-whitelisted trading including via pools actually works — better than Bullish, where AMM/DEX trading is disabled outright.

bearerRedemption.reason: Presenting the token to a third party gets you nothing. Switching between tokenized and nontokenized SECZ runs entirely through Securitize's own platform and requires broker-dealer onboarding: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ', but only holders who 'meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC'. No burn address, no process, no timeframe and no fee is published. A holder outside the whitelist holds a token that is frozen at any new address and convertible nowhere.

forcedTransfers.reason: Verified on-chain 2026-09-16 and corroborated in the filing. The mint carries a PermanentDelegate (D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS) able to transfer or burn from any token account without the holder's signature, a freeze authority able to freeze any account, and PausableConfig able to halt every transfer at once. The S-1 describes the institutional counterpart: Securitize keeps 'manual safeguards ... which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent', and reserves the right in a fork to decide the authoritative record and even to migrate assets. So lost keys, theft, inheritance and court-ordered seizure are all addressable — the property that makes a registered-share tokenization legally usable and that no SPV tracker has.

titleDeed.reason: Stated in a registration statement, which is the strongest form this claim takes anywhere in the universe: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class.' And: 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'; 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. The press release: 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE'; 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share.' No SPV, receipt, derivative or tracker layer. Residual gap: no CUSIP/ISIN is published for the tokenized form and the token metadata carries none, so there is no identifier-level cross-check of the kind the Superstate peer provides.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Self-custody is supported at the mechanism level and this is documented rather than inferred: the Securitize Connect API states that whitelisting a wallet to a token 'does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD', so an arbitrary self-controlled address can be whitelisted directly to hold SECZ, and Securitize's own corporate holdings of Securitize-issued tokenized securities are described as 'held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure'. Caveats: (1) conditional — accounts are frozen at birth and only Securitize's whitelisting makes them usable, and it can re-freeze or pause; (2) the press release describes access as being 'through Securitize's regulated platform' and does not mention self-custody, so how many of the 117 token accounts are genuinely investor-controlled versus platform- or custodian-held is unknown.

issuerIndependent.reason: This is the weakest point in the structure and it is structural, not incidental. Securitize Corp. is simultaneously the securities issuer, the transfer agent, the tokenization platform, the broker-dealer and ATS that gate access, and the holder of the on-chain freeze, claw-back and pause authorities. There is no independent party anywhere — no independent recordkeeping transfer agent as in the Superstate peer, no third-party registrar as at Bullish today. If Securitize stops operating, no address can be thawed, no share can be tokenized or de-tokenized, the control book has no other keeper, and the 'manual safeguards' that back up the chain are its own. The SHARE would survive (Delaware common stock of a reporting company, and a successor transfer agent could be appointed); the TOKEN would not. Note the mitigant on key topology: the mint/freeze authority appears to be a program PDA rather than a plain wallet, which is better than Bullish's funded single key — but a program Securitize controls is still Securitize.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unambiguous and documented in a registration statement: a Delaware corporation, US federal securities law, an SEC-registered transfer agent with a public file number (084-06638), an SEC-registered FINRA-member broker-dealer and ATS gating access, and an NYSE listing. The tokenized form is described in the issuer's own S-1 risk factors rather than only in press releases, which means the legal characterisation is made under Securities Act liability. This is the clearest 'yes' of the three issuers examined and the sharpest contrast with Bullish, which publishes no token instrument at all. The one soft spot is forward-looking rather than present: the S-1 itself notes 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations' for tokenized securities.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent is attached to the token and nothing independent is published about it. The mint's TokenMetadata additionalMetadata array is empty and its update authority is a Securitize-side address; the metadata URI carries name/symbol/description/image only. There is no attestation hook, no proof-of-reserve, no published reconciliation between mint supply and the master securityholder file, no smart-contract audit for the Solana deployment, and no public supply or holder API. The structural problem is worse here than elsewhere: with issuer, transfer agent, platform and broker-dealer all in one group, EVERY assertion about the register is first-party. Securitize's financial statements are audited and it is a reporting company, which is real but is not an attestation about the token.

aiReady.reason: KYC sits directly in the transfer loop, and here it is a broker-dealer's onboarding rather than a platform's: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer', with 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. An autonomous agent cannot complete FINRA-member broker-dealer onboarding. Partial mitigation of the same kind the peer has: whitelisting is per-token and does not require a Securitize iD profile, and on-chain liquidity pools are live, so protocol addresses can evidently be whitelisted — but an agent still cannot get itself whitelisted. Fails on unconditionalTransfers regardless.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: Mechanism, obligation and institutional standing all present. Mechanically: PermanentDelegate, freeze authority and PausableConfig allow seizure, reversal, freezing and a market-wide halt without holder consent. Institutionally: the register is kept by an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638) subject to Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21, and the issuer is a reporting company, so lost-securityholder, escheat and regulatory-request obligations attach. Documented policy: the S-1's fork provisions commit the transfer agent to determine the authoritative record 'for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions', and the manual safeguards exist precisely so that ownership records survive on-chain failure. This is the most explicitly articulated chain-exception posture of the three issuers.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Buyer-and-seller agreement is not sufficient: both sides must be whitelisted to the specific token, and a counterparty must first pass a FINRA-member broker-dealer's onboarding. The press release is explicit that tokenization 'does not ... override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche positions are subject to lock-ups that bind regardless of any agreement between the parties. A trade between two already-whitelisted wallets does settle without per-trade sign-off — and on Solana it can even settle through a liquidity pool, which is more than the Bullish peer allows — but the eligible counterparty set is determined by the issuer's own broker-dealer, and because there is no public allowlist a would-be buyer cannot verify their eligibility in advance.

findings.statement: The issuer of the security, the SEC-registered transfer agent that keeps the register, the platform that mints the token, the broker-dealer and ATS that gate access, and the holder of the on-chain freeze, claw-back and pause authorities are all one corporate group: 'the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration'. Positive: no inter-party reconciliation gap. Negative: every assertion about the register is first-party and the entity holding claw-back power is the company whose shares they are.
findings.quote: As the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration, Securitize uniquely enables a complete lifecycle for tokenized assets.
findings.quoteNote: S-1 p. 10, repeated at pp. 98 and 103. Corroborated by an EDGAR TA-form company search for "securitize" on 2026-09-17, which returns exactly one registrant (Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC, 084-06638) - there is no second, independent transfer agent anywhere in the stack, unlike Bullish, which has two.

findings.statement: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights... Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities.' The tie-break heuristic is the fork recognised by the principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows, and Securitize reserves the right to migrate assets to another fork. Having a policy at all is rarer and better than not having one; the content allocates authority rather than loss, and is decisive evidence against the chain being the main ledger.

issuers.issuingEntity: SHIFT DAO LLC, a for-profit series DAO limited liability company. Each product is a separate designated Series of that LLC (Series 12-18 observed) with its own executed Series Operating Agreement; the Company enters each agreement "solely in its limited and non-discretionary capacity as the administrative agent" and is "not a manager, managing member, fiduciary, or controlling person" of the Series. The initial nominee member of each Series is MINS LLC, Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road, Ajeltake Island, Majuro, MH 96960, which "holds its membership interest solely for purposes of facilitating the formation and annual renewal" and "has no economic entitlement or discretionary authority". The Series 17 agreement is digitally signed 2026-04-19 by Robin Van Niekerk on behalf of MINS LLC. No director, officer or operating-company entity is named; the team page lists twelve individuals with no roles and cites backgrounds at the Israel Securities Authority, Tel-Aviv Stock Exchange, Deloitte, Kraken, Flow Traders, Securitize, CheckPoint, Utila and Emurgo, and names SNZ Holding as seed-round lead investor. The entity that actually holds the backing ETFs is not named: the Solution Overview says only that "SHIFT engages with a private entity that holds the backing assets".
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Republic of the Marshall Islands. Formed under the Decentralized Autonomous Organization Act 2022 and governed under the Limited Liability Company Act 1996, with the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act also cited in the Series agreements. Series segregation is asserted under LLC Act s.79. The Principal Office "need not be in the Marshall Islands" and the "Official Online Venue" for member participation is www.Shiftrwa.xyz.
issuers.governingLaw: Laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, stated in both the Terms of Use (s.12) and each Series Operating Agreement (Art. XII.2). Recourse is narrow: after a 30-day notice period a dispute "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution", seated in the RMI, sole arbitrator, English, final and without appeal, and "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction". The Terms of Use separately submit website disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI". Members owe and are owed no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3, DAO Act s.109), and under Art. VI.2 (DAO Act s.111) "no one shall have the right under the LLC Act to demand to separately inspect or copy records" of the Series.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: Unregistered and self-disclaiming, on top of a real company-law registration. The site-wide legal notice states the tokens "have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933 ... or under the securities or financial-instrument laws of any other jurisdiction", that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State", and that the tokens are "not offered, sold, or distributed in the United States or the United Kingdom, nor to any U.S. or U.K. persons or entities; in applicable jurisdictions they are offered only to 'qualified investors,' 'professional clients,' or their equivalent legal analogues". The Terms of Use add that the membership interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law, but purchasers are responsible for assessing their legal status in their jurisdiction". No licence, prospectus, offering document or exemption filing was located in any jurisdiction.
issuers.holderClaim: On paper: a membership interest in a designated Series of SHIFT DAO LLC whose sole purpose is to "acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to" one named index or stock. The Series 17 agreement says "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 says "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", with no voting, management or fiduciary rights. In practice three things break that chain. (1) The issuer's own site-wide legal notice says the opposite: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." (2) The executed Series agreements do not identify the token they govern - membership is obtained by holding a token "created from and constricted by the parameters defined in the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined" - so no published document links the SPL mint that trades on Jupiter to the Series whose treasury holds the asset; the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement compounds this by requiring "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". (3) What the Series is documented to hold is not the referenced equity but a daily-reset leveraged ETF share (Series 17: SPXL, Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3x, ISIN US25459W8626; Series 12: Direxion Daily TSLA X2, ISIN US25460G2865), so exposure to Tesla or the S&P 500 is delivered through a third party's derivative fund. Graded as derivative for that reason; if the Series agreements' "owners in the Series Assets" language controlled and were bound to these mints, the record would move to spv-claim-redeemable.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: Two custodians are named, in the Risk Disclosure only: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets." The Collateral & Custody page adds that backing is held "with FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners" in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" and "off-balance-sheet". Marketing and press name Alpaca Markets as the brokerage rail. The holding entity itself is not named ("a private entity that holds the backing assets"), nor is the market maker that operates the B2B mint/burn endpoints, and no account, statement, holdings report or balance for any Series has been published.

custodyVerification.agent: Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves is claimed as the verification agent; no feed, contract or report was located
custodyVerification.frequency: claimed continuous - "The feed publishes the verified reserve state on-chain, every block" - but nothing observed at any cadence
custodyVerification.notes: Claimed, not evidenced. The docs assert Chainlink PoR "runs continuously, verifying that every Series Token in circulation is backed 1:1" and that "the SHIFT smart contract cannot issue tokens in excess of verified reserves; mint operations are gated by PoR feed". Verified 2026-09-16 and re-verified 2026-09-17: the PoR dashboard link on that same page still reads "[TO BE UPDATED]" and the third-party attestation section still reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", and no Chainlink PoR feed naming SHIFT could be found. The app dashboard link has changed: on 2026-09-16 the page pointed to https://app.shiftrwa.xyz, which redirected to /coming-soon; on 2026-09-17 the page points to shift-rwa.vercel.app/app, and both https://shift-rwa.vercel.app/app and https://app.shiftrwa.xyz/ return HTTP 200 client-rendered pages. Neither publishes a reserve figure: the Vercel app renders "TSL2L $0.00" and "TSL1S $0.00" under Top Movers, and app.shiftrwa.xyz returns an empty SPA shell. The earlier marketing site states PoR is "coming with mainnet". The on-chain record contradicts the gating claim outright: every observed issuance is a bare SPL Token-2022 mintTo signed by the mint's own authority keypair plus a fee payer, with no SHIFT program, oracle account or PoR account in the transaction at all.

securityInterest.holder: none - no charge, pledge, lien or security agent is created; the Series is documented as owning its treasury outright under LLC Act s.79 segregation

redemption.eligibility: Contradicted between primary documents. Each Series Operating Agreement grants a member a redemption right: "If a Member wishes to transfer their token back to the Series in exchange for funds, this is an internal membership-interest repurchase ... This transaction is available only to Members processed by smart contract where the transaction is settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet, not using any third-party assets." The Technical Overview says the opposite: "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly. Mint and burn are B2B endpoints used by professional market makers to maintain inventory. Users acquire Series Tokens by swapping on Jupiter against market-maker liquidity." U.S. and U.K. persons are excluded from membership entirely.
redemption.rails: Documented retail path: internal membership-interest repurchase settled from the Series treasury by smart contract. Documented operational path: market makers mint and burn against the underlying ETF through B2B endpoints, 24/5 in line with U.S. trading hours, while user-facing trading is 24/7 RFQ on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. No burn address, latency, SLA or minimum is published for either path, and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to implement the smart-contract repurchase.
redemption.fees: Primary market: "The per-token purchase price shall equal the executed market price paid in a bona fide transaction to acquire one (1) share of [the named ETF], plus a transaction fee equal to 0.1% of such executed price." Ongoing: "The Master DAO is allowed to charge operational fees to the Series using a percentage-of-treasury formula" - the percentage is never stated in the master or any Series agreement. Secondary market: "User-facing trading costs are reflected in the RFQ spread quoted by market makers", tightest in U.S. hours and widest at weekends; the two docs pages give different weekend ceilings ("up to ~3%" in Solution Overview, "up to ~5%" in Risk Management). No transfer fee is charged on-chain: none of the eight mints carries a transferFeeConfig extension.

issuers.corporateActions: Nothing is passed through and nothing is applied by Shift. "Membership interests represent a limited economic interest in the Assets of the Series 17 treasury and do not provide any expectation of profit, income, or dividends." Leverage resets are the ETF issuer's: "SHIFT does not perform rebalancing. The leverage is delivered by the underlying ETF (e.g., Direxion TSLL), which manages its own daily reset internally. SHIFT simply tokenizes the ETF position 1:1. Nothing happens at 4 PM ET inside the SHIFT protocol." Wind-down is issuer-decided: on a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone determines, in its administrative capacity, whether each Series "(i) continue[s] as an independent DAO LLC" or "(ii) be dissolved and wound up", and "all applicable fees, costs, and third-party expenses associated with such continuation shall be borne by the applicable Series or its members". Membership can also end involuntarily - "the person's involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal of their status as a Member, if the person is deemed a Restricted Person" - and Art. VII.2 provides that voluntary or involuntary cessation "does not give rise to any right of a Member to a distribution of any property or economic resources". Separately, the scaledUiAmountConfig authority on every mint lets the issuer restate all displayed balances; SOX3S already sits at multiplier 0.1.

pricing.notes: The issuer publishes no NAV, mark or indicative value for any Series Token at any cadence, and no oracle carries a price for them (rwa-sonar's own reference-price probe returns refSource null for all 8: "leveraged; no 1:1 reference"; the Shift symbols also truncate their underlyings, TSL2L to TSL and SOX3L to SOX, so no ticker join is possible). The user-facing price is a market maker's RFQ quote "based on the underlying ETF's NAV, plus a spread", and the spread is neither published nor bounded in any document. The primary-market price is anchored to a real exchange print - the executed price of one share of the named Direxion ETF plus 0.1% - so arbitrage against a public NAV is structurally possible, but only for the authorized market makers who can reach the mint/burn endpoints, and only 24/5. Observed secondary market on 2026-09-16: Jupiter reports null DEX liquidity on all eight mints, USD 117.91 of total 24h volume across all of them, organicScore 0 on every one, and a first pool for only 3 of 8 (all created 2026-07-31).

openQuestions: Which document controls? The executed Series agreements say "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and grant "treasury ownership only", while the site-wide legal notice says holding the tokens gives no "legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets". The whole claim-depth grade turns on this and the issuer publishes both.

Which mint does each Series Operating Agreement actually govern? Every agreement locates the token in "the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined", and the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement requires "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". Nothing published links the mints that trade to the Series that hold the assets.

What backs SPCX2L and SPCX2S, and under what Series? Both mints are live and trading, neither appears in the docs' Series or contract-address tables, and no Operating Agreement exists. Direxion's 2x SpaceX bull ETF (LOFF) listed on NYSE Arca on 15 June per Structured Retail Products, and a bear counterpart (LOFD) was announced later - was either instrument held when 250 SPCX2L were minted on 2026-06-16 and 395.72 SPCX2S on 2026-06-24?

Does the Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves integration exist at all? The docs describe it as gating every mint and publishing every block; the dashboard link is "[TO BE UPDATED]", no feed naming SHIFT was found, and no observed mint transaction touches an oracle account.

Is there any SHIFT Solana program? The docs describe "the SHIFT Solana program" that "mints, burns, and tracks Series Token supply" and audited "open-source" contracts, but every observed issuance is a raw Token-2022 mintTo signed by a bare keypair.
What is ARTokens GmbH to SHIFT DAO LLC, and why is its June 2025 Ethereum ERC-20 audit the only file on Shift's Audits page?
Why is SOX3S on a scaled-UI multiplier of 0.1 when the other seven mints are on 1? No document mentions the multiplier.
What is the Master DAO's percentage-of-treasury fee? Both the master and the Series agreements authorise it and neither states a number.

Which restriction list binds? The Series agreements define Restricted Persons as UN-listed persons plus residents of Iran, Syria, Cuba, North Korea and Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk, and do not exclude U.S. or U.K. persons - while the Terms of Use, Risk Disclosure and site notice exclude them explicitly and threaten "immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation". The binding agreement and the marketed policy differ.

Where did "over $40M in liquidity" go? Press reporting from the June 2026 Jupiter listing cites that figure; on 2026-09-16 Jupiter reports no DEX liquidity on any Shift mint, USD 3.26M of combined market cap and USD 117.91 of 24h volume.

Is the leveraged programme still being invested in, or is it being succeeded? www.shiftrwa.xyz now leads with covered-call vaults on SPY and COPX while /faq, /markets, /blog, /status and the Operating Agreement PDFs 404 on that domain and survive only on a Vercel preview host.
Who is the market maker with mint and burn access, and who is the "private entity that holds the backing assets"? Neither is named, and both sit between the holder and the ETF.
