keyGovernance.evidence: Verified 2026-09-16 by RPC. Each mint has its own single authority address that simultaneously holds mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate, metadataUpdateAuthority, pause and scaled-UI authority (SPX3L CoghvrToe8SZTta5Q6cb2BnVki6WXXGMogeSiea5vNte; SPX3S 2CeU1GEWbhXXZvypMfAPa2AzyvF3yhrG7AqUyFoDqxZf; TSL2L 21bymdv3CB8QFa5taouuTcrgTVLjH9vKVEScEKqKGRZd; TSL1S 9eo5QkvdxsAU6kdAbAABWpbq1TGvsxPkLoroPwgxY4o1; SOX3L 2g5JvVx2C6si9XoLoMjr1CEyK8Mt597qptsrNN1RZ4WB; SOX3S 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA; SPCX2L ELt7GJcL4jxVoF1snNjxjegPKjuELxi13ut5f8R7vgH; SPCX2S 4mU3jH1iEA78LJ9YPfFYnN4ABty6xMBxndajFg3iToaK). getMultipleAccounts returns null for all eight, i.e. they are unfunded, dataless addresses, and each one nevertheless appears as a true transaction signer on raw Token-2022 mintTo instructions with a separate funded fee payer (2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz) - so they are plain off-chain Ed25519 keypairs, not program-derived addresses (a PDA cannot sign at the transaction level) and not Squads or any other multisig (no multisig program appears in any of the transactions). Recorded as hot-key with that nuance: single-key control, fees sponsored by another wallet. The mints themselves were created on 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-11 by HJfhNwwaDqcUc7k5J8N5y3y1xHZ7qDYMsC7YFpp9fCdp with a plain createAccount + initialize* + setAuthority script. No threshold, timelock or governance process is disclosed for any of these keys, and none of the eight addresses appears in any Shift document.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Membership is defined by token holding: "A person becomes a Member by obtaining at least one (1) [Series] SHFT Token", and each holder "shall be deemed to have agreed to and be bound by this Agreement upon such person's acquiring" it. The Series records required by Art. VI.1 are "the name of each current and former Member or the unique Distributed Ledger identifier(s) attributable to each Member", and where the activity is on a distributed ledger with public human-readable explanations "there shall be no separate requirement to keep books of accounts". No transfer agent, share register or off-chain holder list exists anywhere in the documents. The caveat that keeps this from being clean: the agreements never name the mint, locating the token smart contract at "an address and a blockchain to be determined", so the chain is the register of a Series whose own agreement does not identify which chain or which mint.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Nothing gates a transfer today, on any of the eight mints: defaultAccountState is initialized (new accounts are not frozen), the transferHook slot is initialized with a null programId, there is no allowlist, and there is no transferFeeConfig at all. Any wallet can send to any wallet, and the tokens are marketed as "24/7 permissionless" and composable on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. Control is entirely reactive: the permanentDelegate, freeze and pause powers are exercised after the fact, and the Risk Disclosure says a U.S. or U.K. person who bypasses the restrictions "may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse".

bearerRedemption.reason: Presenting the token compels delivery from nobody. The Series Operating Agreement's repurchase right is to be "processed by smart contract", and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to process it - every observed issuance is a raw Token-2022 mintTo by a keypair. The Technical Overview states plainly that "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly" and that mint and burn are "B2B endpoints used by professional market makers", the app that would front a redemption resolves to /coming-soon, backing operations run only 24/5, and U.S. and U.K. persons are barred from membership entirely. Observed burns are negligible: on SOX3L the sum of all mintTo amounts (3,967.41007219) exceeds current supply (3,967.37399156) by 0.03608063 tokens, i.e. about 0.0009% of supply has ever been retired.

forcedTransfers.reason: Confirmed in both law and code. All eight mints carry a live permanentDelegate plus freezeAuthority and pausableConfig, all three held by the same single key per mint. The Risk Disclosure authorises the use: any attempt by a U.S. or U.K. person to bypass the restrictions "including the use of VPNs or proxy entities - is a material breach of the Operational Agreement and may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse", and Art. VII of each Series agreement makes Restricted-Person status trigger "involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal" of membership with no right to a distribution.

titleDeed.reason: The site-wide legal notice is explicit: holding the tokens "does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets", and each Series "is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by" the trademark owners it references. Even on the Series agreements' more generous reading ("treasury ownership only"), the treasury asset is a Direxion daily-reset leveraged ETF share, not the referenced equity, so the token is at best a derived interest two layers away from Tesla or the S&P 500.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Ordinary Token-2022 mints, held in any Solana wallet: "Holders custody the token in any Solana wallet. There is no liquidation engine and no forced close", and "SPL tokens held in any Solana wallet. No exchange custody." No KYC or allowlist gates holding, and Phantom, OKX Wallet and other wallets are listed integrations.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token cannot outlive its administrator on its own terms. On a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone decides whether each Series continues as an independent DAO LLC or is wound up, and the members pay for continuation. The documented value chain runs entirely through parties the holder cannot reach: an unnamed "private entity that holds the backing assets", unnamed market makers who alone can mint and burn, and an administrator that owes no fiduciary duty and is subject to no court action in any jurisdiction. Nothing independent of Shift attests the reserve, and no NAV or PoR feed exists to price the token if Shift stopped publishing.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unusually well pinned down for this cohort. A named issuer (SHIFT DAO LLC), a named jurisdiction (Republic of the Marshall Islands, DAO Act 2022 and LLC Act 1996), a stated governing law (RMI, in both the Terms of Use and every Series agreement), a named nominee member with a Majuro address (MINS LLC, Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road) and a fixed forum (ICDR arbitration seated in the RMI). The flag asks whether the jurisdiction is preset, and it is; what the jurisdiction is worth is another matter, since the agreements bar any court action anywhere and remove both fiduciary duties and inspection rights.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Every third-party verification Shift claims is either absent or somebody else's. Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves is described as running "continuously" and publishing "every block" and as gating mints, yet the PoR dashboard link reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", no Chainlink PoR feed naming SHIFT could be located, and the observed mints carry no oracle account at all. The "Third-party attestation" heading in the Collateral & Custody page is an empty "[TO BE UPDATED]". The sole file on the Audits page is a Zokyo review of ARTokens GmbH's Ethereum ERC-20 contract dated 19 June 2025. No custodian confirmation, holdings statement or reconciliation output has ever been published by DekaBank, ALPACADB LTD or anyone else.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers is yes and tokenSelfCustody is yes, so an agent can hold and trade these tokens with no KYC and no allowlist. Three caveats that the flag does not capture: an agent cannot truthfully make the non-U.S./non-U.K.-person representation membership requires, it holds an asset subject to clawback, freeze and global pause by a single key, and there is effectively no market to trade into - USD 117.91 of 24h volume across all eight mints and no reported DEX liquidity on any of them.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The mechanism exists but no document binds it to a legal process. The clawback, freeze and pause powers are triggered by the issuer's own determination - Restricted-Person status or "a material breach of the Operational Agreement" such as VPN use - not by a court or regulator, and no procedure, notice period or appeal is published. The Restricted-Person definition does track external legal instruments (the UN Security Council Consolidated List and OFAC-embargoed regions), which is the one point in Shift's favour, but the same agreements bar any court action "in any court of any jurisdiction" and remove inspection rights, so there is no ordinary forum in which a holder-facing order could be obtained and then reflected on-chain.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A DEX or peer-to-peer transfer settles on the agreement of buyer and seller alone: no issuer signature, allowlist check, transfer hook or KYC step sits in the transfer path on any of the eight mints. Validity can be undone afterwards by clawback or freeze, but the transfer itself needs no third party.

attestations.quote: Single source of truth for SHIFT DAO LLC's policies, disclosures, and the Operating Agreements governing each Series of membership-interest tokens.
attestations.statement: A full legal set is published and was retrieved on 2026-09-16: Terms of Use, Risk Disclosure, FAQ, Privacy Policy, the Master Operating Agreement and executed Series Operating Agreements for Series 12, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 18. The GitBook legal hub is described as the "Single source of truth for SHIFT DAO LLC's policies, disclosures, and the Operating Agreements governing each Series of membership-interest tokens" and was last updated 7 days before this review.

attestations.quote: The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets.
attestations.statement: Site-wide legal notice: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." The Series agreements add "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only. Members shall have no voting rights, management rights, or authority to participate in the control or operation of the Series", and the FAQ: "A Series membership grants you an exclusive economic interest in the assets held by the Series treasury, but it does not include voting or management rights."

attestations.quote: Any attempt by a U.S. or U.K. person to bypass these restrictions — including the use of VPNs or proxy entities — is a material breach of the Operational Agreement and may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse.
attestations.statement: Risk Disclosure: any attempt by a U.S. or U.K. person to bypass the eligibility restrictions "including the use of VPNs or proxy entities - is a material breach of the Operational Agreement and may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse". On-chain on 2026-09-16 every one of the eight mints carries permanentDelegate, freezeAuthority, mintAuthority and pausableConfig, all held by one key per mint.

attestations.quote: Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets.
attestations.statement: Risk Disclosure: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets", held in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" with "FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners". Recorded unknown: neither named firm has published any confirmation, account statement or holdings report tied to these Series, the entity that actually holds the ETFs is described only as "a private entity", and no Series is identified in any custodian document.

attestations.quote: WHEREAS, Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets and can be members of the Master DAO, and members of the Master DAO can also be members of Series 17 and other Series;
attestations.statement: Series 17 Operating Agreement: "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", each Series "acting functionally as its own LLC with distinct assets, liabilities, and objectives" under LLC Act s.79. Recorded unknown because the issuer's own site-wide notice denies exactly this ("does not grant ... legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets") and because the agreement does not identify the mint it governs ("an address and a blockchain to be determined"), so the traded SPL token cannot be shown to be the membership interest described.

attestations.quote: Series Token contract addresses on Solana. Always verify the address before any swap or wallet addition.
attestations.statement: The docs publish a Contract addresses table with the Solana SPL address for six of the eight live mints (TSL2L, TSL1S, SOX3L, SOX3S, SPX3L, SPX3S), all of which match the mints observed on-chain, with the instruction "Always verify the address before any swap or wallet addition." The two SpaceX mints that exist and trade (SPCX2L, SPCX2S) are absent from this table and from the Product Overview Series table.

attestations.quote: For every Series Token in circulation, this entity holds the corresponding leveraged or inverse ETF on a 1:1 basis. Backing assets are acquired through regulated brokerage rails connected via API. There are no fractional reserves. Tokens cannot be issued in excess of verified backing.
attestations.statement: Solution Overview: "For every Series Token in circulation, this entity holds the corresponding leveraged or inverse ETF on a 1:1 basis ... There are no fractional reserves. Tokens cannot be issued in excess of verified backing." Recorded unknown: no proof-of-reserve feed, attestation, custodian confirmation or holdings report exists, the claimed Chainlink PoR gating is absent from every observed mint transaction, and the SPCX2S mint was issued while the issuer's own pages said the underlying instrument was not yet available.

findings.quote: → Proof-of-Reserves dashboard [TO BE UPDATED]
findings.statement: 1:1 backing is the central product claim and nothing verifies it. Chainlink PoR is said to run "continuously" and publish "the verified reserve state on-chain, every block" while gating mints, but the PoR dashboard link on that page is "[TO BE UPDATED]", the "Third-party attestation" section is "[TO BE UPDATED]", the app dashboard it points to resolves to /coming-soon, no Chainlink feed naming SHIFT could be located, and no custodian statement or holdings report has ever been published.

findings.quote: All SHIFT smart contracts are audited by independent third-party security firms. Audit reports are published in full and updated as the protocol expands.
findings.statement: The Audits page claims "All SHIFT smart contracts are audited by independent third-party security firms" and links a single file: ARTokens_GmbH_Zokyo_audit_report_June19_2025.pdf, a Zokyo review of ARTokens GmbH scoped to "aRtoken.sol" from repo github.com/artokens-fi/art-erc20 at commit 93e33c9a45fec14c2b611c4c49b8a504fd96cf77, written against "the Ethereum network's" environment and dated 19 June 2025. It names no SHIFT entity, no Solana program and no Token-2022 mint, and there is no SHIFT program on Solana for it to have audited.

findings.quote: getMultipleAccounts on the eight mint authorities returns null for all eight (no account, no lamports, no data)
findings.statement: Each mint's mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate, metadata, pause and scaled-UI authority is one and the same address, and that address signs raw SPL Token-2022 mintTo instructions directly with no multisig program anywhere in the transaction. The eight authority addresses hold no lamports and no data, so they are plain off-chain keypairs with fees sponsored by 2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz. No threshold, quorum or timelock is disclosed in any Shift document. Verified by getMultipleAccounts over all eight authority addresses and getTransaction on their mintTo signatures.

findings.quote: Series Token contract addresses on Solana. Always verify the address before any swap or wallet addition.
findings.statement: None of the eight keys that can claw back, freeze or pause a Shift mint appears in any published Shift document, and no role, entity or governance process is attached to them. The docs publish mint addresses but never the authorities that control them.

findings.quote: pausableConfig: {authority: CoghvrToe8SZTta5Q6cb2BnVki6WXXGMogeSiea5vNte, paused: false}
findings.statement: All eight mints carry pausableConfig with a live authority (paused=false on 2026-09-16), so one key per product can halt every transfer of that token at once, with no court, regulator or notice period involved. The product is marketed as "24/7 permissionless".

findings.quote: scaledUiAmountConfig: {authority: 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA, multiplier: 0.1} on SOX3S; multiplier: 1 on the other seven mints
findings.statement: Every Shift mint carries scaledUiAmountConfig under the same single authority, so all displayed balances can be restated by changing one multiplier. This is not hypothetical: SOX3S already sits at multiplier 0.1 while the other seven are at 1, and no Shift document mentions the multiplier, explains the SOX3S value or commits to a notice period for changing it.

findings.quote: mintTo: {amount: 39571858898, mint: FtBpBcLU4Epjm2nnuQNRYGkFM6jfsXrcGKJSiKCtSHFT, mintAuthority: 4mU3jH1iEA78LJ9YPfFYnN4ABty6xMBxndajFg3iToaK}; instructions: ComputeBudget, AToken createIdempotent, Token-2022 mintTo (no program, oracle or reserve account)
findings.statement: Issuance is unconditioned. 395.71858898 SPCX2S were minted on 2026-06-24 while the issuer's own markets page carried SPCX2S as not yet tradable and a June 2026 report said its launch was "subject to the availability of the underlying market instrument"; no Series Operating Agreement for a SpaceX Series has ever been published. Every observed mintTo is a bare Token-2022 instruction signed by a keypair, with no program, oracle or reserve account in the transaction, so the claim that "tokens cannot be issued in excess of verified backing" has no on-chain enforcement.

findings.quote: Each Series of SHIFT DAO LLC operates under its own dedicated Operating Agreement, issued under the Marshall Islands DAO LLC Act. Final executed copies are linked below; additional Series are posted here as they go live.
findings.statement: Two of the eight live mints have no terms at all. The operating-agreements page publishes the master agreement plus Series 12, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 18; SPCX2L and SPCX2S are covered by no agreement, appear in neither the Product Overview Series table nor the Contract addresses table, and therefore have no documented Series, no defined permitted Assets, no price formula and no redemption right - while trading on Jupiter under the Shift name and tag.

findings.quote: WHEREAS, Series 17 is designated solely to acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to the S&P 500® index (the “Assets”), as established and approved by the Master DAO.
findings.statement: The Series agreements define the treasury contents openly: Series 17 is "designated solely to acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to the S&P 500 index (the 'Assets'), as established and approved by the Master DAO", and "The Master DAO shall define via its own governance process, which asset the Series acquires and holds". A specific ETF (SPXL, ISIN US25459W8626) is named only in the pricing formula, not as a binding holdings constraint, so the Series is not contractually confined to the instrument the marketing names.

findings.quote: End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly. Mint and burn are B2B endpoints used by professional market makers to maintain inventory.
findings.statement: The Series agreements grant a member redemption "processed by smart contract ... settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet", while the Technical Overview says "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly" and mint/burn are "B2B endpoints used by professional market makers". No SHIFT program exists on-chain to process a member repurchase, the app front-end is at /coming-soon, and observed net burns are negligible (SOX3L: total minted 3,967.41007219 versus supply 3,967.37399156, a net 0.03608063 tokens retired).

findings.quote: Weekends Widest (up to ~3%) No primary-market access for two days; inventory cannot be replenished or hedged
findings.statement: The docs acknowledge the gap - "Backing operations (ETF purchases) run 24/5, in line with U.S. trading hours. User-facing trading on Jupiter remains 24/7" - but state no latency, SLA or bound for mint, burn or redemption, and the two pages disagree on the resulting cost: weekend spreads "Widest (up to ~3%)" in Solution Overview against "up to ~5%" in Risk Management.

findings.quote: Shift — trade tokenized stocks and ETFs with built-in 2x and 3x leverage, long or short, on-chain. No forced liquidations.
findings.statement: Shift publishes no NAV, indicative value or valuation output for any Series Token at any cadence. The markets page shows "Loading live price..." and "On-chain TVL feed wires up next, with the indexer", the app dashboard is /coming-soon, and the only price a holder can see is a market maker's RFQ quote whose spread is neither published nor bounded.

findings.quote: 67 tickers match no Pyth feed (BRK.B, many ETFs, Shift-truncated SOX/TSL/SPX).
findings.statement: No oracle publisher carries a price for any Shift mint. The Shift symbols truncate their underlyings (TSL2L to TSL, SOX3L to SOX, SPX3L to SPX), so no Pyth equity feed matches, and the repo's own probe resolves all eight to refSource null with the note "leveraged; no 1:1 reference" (stocks/data/reference-prices.json). On-chain consumers such as the lending venues the docs name have no attested feed to read.

Jupiter reports null DEX liquidity for all eight mints against USD 3,260,945 of combined market cap, with a first pool for only three of them (all created 2026-07-31) and USD 117.91 of total 24h volume across the whole issuer - against press reporting of "over $40M in liquidity" assembled by Shift RWA. SPX3L alone accounts for USD 81.79 of that volume; four of the eight traded nothing. Aggregated from stocks/data/universe.json (Jupiter lite-api tokens/v2/search, fetched 2026-09-16T14:02:53Z).

findings.quote: "organicScore":0,"organicScoreLabel":"low","isVerified":true,"tags":["verified","stocks","shift","rwa","token-2022"]
findings.statement: Jupiter reports organicScore 0 and organicScoreLabel "low" on all eight mints, with buyOrganicVolume and sellOrganicVolume null throughout, so no part of the reported 24h volume is measured as organic end-holder flow. Trader counts are 0 to 2 per token per day. Read from stocks/data/universe.json, fetched 2026-09-16T14:02:53Z.

findings.quote: Holder concentration (Jupiter audit.topHoldersPercentage, median per issuer): xStocks 99.9%, Ondo 98.4%, Shift 99.9%, PreStocks 56.2%, Tessera 16.7%, Backpack 12.9%
findings.statement: Median top-10 holder share is 99.79% across the eight mints (99.86% SPX3L, 99.93% SPX3S, 99.20% TSL2L, 99.95% SOX3S, 99.72% SOX3L, 99.92% TSL1S, and the lower 81.39% SPCX2L and 95.78% SPCX2S), so the 1,810 reported holder accounts do not measure distribution - essentially all supply sits in issuer or market-maker inventory wallets.

findings.quote: In extreme cases, some or all of the Series Assets may become unrecoverable.
findings.statement: Inter-Series segregation is asserted "To the maximum extent permitted by the LLC Act" and the FAQ says "The debts of one Series cannot legally affect another", but no insolvency or trust-recognition opinion is published for the RMI series structure or for the off-chain holding arrangement, and the Risk Disclosure concedes that on custodian insolvency "In extreme cases, some or all of the Series Assets may become unrecoverable."

findings.quote: holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets
findings.statement: On the issuer's own site-wide notice the holder has no proprietary claim: holding the tokens "does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets". The Series agreements reinforce the downside - dissolution distributes only "after settling all debts", and cessation of member status, including involuntary withdrawal, "does not give rise to any right of a Member to a distribution of any property or economic resources". No security interest, trustee or collateral agent exists.

findings.quote: IV.3 No fiduciary duties unless expressly approved. In accordance with §109 of the DAO Act, no Member shall have any fiduciary duty to the Company or any Member unless otherwise provided for in this Agreement or any governance rules approved in accordance with this Agreement.
findings.statement: SHIFT DAO LLC is the issuer of every Series, its sole administrator, the party that "shall define which asset the Series acquires and holds", the recipient of an undisclosed percentage-of-treasury fee, and the holder of every on-chain authority. The only other parties in the agreements are a nominee member with "no economic entitlement or discretionary authority" and an unnamed "private entity that holds the backing assets"; the docs also state the Master DAO "does not serve as a manager, investment adviser, or fiduciary", so no independent party assures anything about the reserve or the register.

findings.quote: This requires timely and accurate reconciliation between on-chain token activity and off-chain activity, including acquisitions and disposals of off-chain assets linked to new issuances or redemptions.
findings.statement: The Risk Disclosure commits each Series to the obligation - "This requires timely and accurate reconciliation between on-chain token activity and off-chain activity, including acquisitions and disposals of off-chain assets linked to new issuances or redemptions" - and warns that failure "may result in imbalances". No reconciliation report, supply endpoint or per-Series holdings figure has ever been published, so the claim cannot be tested from outside.

findings.quote: These interests do not constitute public securities under RMI law, but purchasers are responsible for assessing their legal status in their jurisdiction.
findings.statement: A real company-law registration is presented alongside express denials of regulated status. The Terms of Use lean on the RMI DAO LLC registration for "legal clarity" while stating the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law", and the site notice adds that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State". A series vehicle that holds an ETF against redeemable interests is fund-shaped; no fund authorisation exists anywhere.

keyGovernance.evidence: Verified 2026-09-16 by RPC. Each mint has its own single authority address that simultaneously holds mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate, metadataUpdateAuthority, pause and scaled-UI authority (SPX3L CoghvrToe8SZTta5Q6cb2BnVki6WXXGMogeSiea5vNte; SPX3S 2CeU1GEWbhXXZvypMfAPa2AzyvF3yhrG7AqUyFoDqxZf; TSL2L 21bymdv3CB8QFa5taouuTcrgTVLjH9vKVEScEKqKGRZd; TSL1S 9eo5QkvdxsAU6kdAbAABWpbq1TGvsxPkLoroPwgxY4o1; SOX3L 2g5JvVx2C6si9XoLoMjr1CEyK8Mt597qptsrNN1RZ4WB; SOX3S 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA; SPCX2L ELt7GJcL4jxVoF1snNjxjegPKjuELxi13ut5f8R7vgH; SPCX2S 4mU3jH1iEA78LJ9YPfFYnN4ABty6xMBxndajFg3iToaK). getMultipleAccounts returns null for all eight, i.e. they are unfunded, dataless addresses, and each one nevertheless appears as a true transaction signer on raw Token-2022 mintTo instructions with a separate funded fee payer (2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz) - so they are plain off-chain Ed25519 keypairs, not program-derived addresses (a PDA cannot sign at the transaction level) and not Squads or any other multisig (no multisig program appears in any of the transactions). Recorded as hot-key with that nuance: single-key control, fees sponsored by another wallet. The mints themselves were created on 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-11 by HJfhNwwaDqcUc7k5J8N5y3y1xHZ7qDYMsC7YFpp9fCdp with a plain createAccount + initialize* + setAuthority script. No threshold, timelock or governance process is disclosed for any of these keys, and none of the eight addresses appears in any Shift document.

custodyVerification.notes: SYSTEMATIC RECONCILIATION BREAK FOUND (2026-09-16, all four Solana equities compared): Superstate's public API circulating-supply exceeds the on-chain Token-2022 mint supply by exactly 0.1 shares on FWDI (api 7,280,819.200000 vs chain 7,280,819.100000) and on GLXY (api 13,399.282876 vs chain 13,399.182876), and matches exactly on EXOD (60.000000) and HSDT (0). The +0.1 appears on precisely the two tickers with a DeFi integration, and the FWDI asset page exposes an 'AdminSeed-Kamino-SolMainnet-900' position worth 0.607498 notional = 0.1 share at $6.07 — so the most likely reading is an admin seed counted in the register figure but absent from the mint supply, not random drift. Superstate's own rendered FWDI asset page shows 7,280,819.10 on Solana, agreeing with the chain and disagreeing with its own API. Economically trivial (~$0.61) but structurally the point: the chain is a mirror of the register, the mirror is measurably and repeatably off, two Superstate surfaces disagree with each other, and no published reconciliation would have caught it. There are FOUR machine-readable verification surfaces, all public and unauthenticated: (1) https://api.superstate.com/v2/instruments returns, per ticker, the CUSIP, the per-chain mint address, total_supply, circulating_supply, the equity burn address and the split multiplier — verified 2026-09-16: FWDI total_supply 8,723,436.10 (the dossier previously recorded 8,732,937.10, a transcription error: it does not reconcile with the same-day 7,280,819.20 tokenized + 1,442,616.90 book-entry), circulating (tokenized) 7,280,819.20; (2) per-ticker scalar endpoints https://api.superstate.com/v1/instruments/FWDI/total-supply and /circulating-supply (plain numbers, no auth); (3) the Token-2022 mint itself via getTokenSupply — FWDI 7,280,819.100000 at slot 447531447; (4) the Allowlist program HFkKyweJDUuGer5KaCst5qZSYD5aapKaD7xzdNaoRtfA is publicly enumerable — getProgramAccounts returned 827 accounts (698 of 32 bytes, 129 of 64 bytes) on 2026-09-16, and Superstate publishes a Rust SDK (crates.io superstate-allowlist-interface) and TS SDK (@superstateinc/allowlist) to read its state. 481 Token-2022 accounts exist for the FWDI mint. What is NOT public: the register itself (holder identities, name/address/TIN), which sits in Superstate's Subsidiary Securityholder Records and the RTA's Master Securityholder File. Superstate's /v1/balances and /v2/transactions APIs require an API key scoped to your own entity; the issuer sees a private 'Issuance dashboard'. No auditor attestation, no Chainlink Proof-of-Reserve and no reconciliation report on the equities is published. Reserve-style verification is structurally unnecessary — the token is the share, not a claim on a reserve.

redemption.eligibility: Any allowlisted holder with an approved Superstate account. 'Burn to book-entry' converts tokens back to book-entry shares; those can then be DRS-transferred to a traditional brokerage and sold on Nasdaq. Available to eligible investors globally ('Global*', excluding jurisdictions subject to US sanctions); accredited-investor status is NOT required.
redemption.rails: Send tokens to the published equity burn address on Solana (2u8YwJTykTreziHBN5QwE7Bi2SyN8M2MicCscthtph9E — the same burn address for all Solana equities), then the book-entry balance updates in the Superstate portal; a transfer authorization form plus a DRS transfer moves the shares to a broker. Note: burning equity tokens does NOT trigger a cash payout (unlike the funds) — you must sell on a DEX or move the shares to a broker to realise value.
redemption.fees: Superstate charges no processing fee for burn/transfer; the holder pays Solana network fees and any fees charged by the Recordkeeping Transfer Agent or the receiving broker-dealer (Terms §4.2, §4.3).

issuers.corporateActions: Dividends: on Board declaration the issuer instructs the RTA with declaration/ex/record/payment dates and amount per share; payment is 'in cash or additional Shares (or other agreed to form, such as stablecoins, in the future), at the election of each shareholder' and Superstate coordinates with the RTA to process dividends, payments and tax forms (Digital Transfer Agency Agreement Schedule A §4). Note that FWDI, GLXY, EXOD and HSDT do not currently pay dividends, so the pathway is untested in practice. Voting/proxy: the tokenized holder is a holder of record, and Superstate 'will coordinate with the RTA to enable shareholder communication and proxy material distribution' (Schedule A §3.3); there is no on-chain voting. Splits: applied at the mint via the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount multiplier, and exposed publicly as equity_info.current_split_multiplier in the instruments API. Lost shareholders: Superstate performs Rule 17Ad-17 services; escheat stays with the issuer/RTA (Schedule A §5).

pricing.notes: The underlying class trades on Nasdaq, so an exchange price exists, but the TOKEN has no exchange venue. Forward Industries' own 10-K warns that 'there are no current trading venues for the tokenized shares' and holders 'may face potential illiquidity, trading volatility and/or pricing discrepancies when compared to shares of common stock which trade on Nasdaq. These discrepancies may be substantial.' Arbitrage exists but is slow and one-way-ish: conversion of tokens back to Nasdaq-tradeable book-entry shares 'could take up to multiple weeks' (10-K), which is far too slow to hold the peg intraday. Solana Company's 10-K makes the same point: 'prolonged price discrepancies between Tokenized and Traditional HSDT — especially where arbitrage is limited by operational or regulatory constraints.' Superstate publishes two Pyth feeds per equity: a Nasdaq feed (Equity.US.FWDI/USD) and a Superstate index feed used by DeFi protocols (Crypto.Index.FWDI/USD); the Direct Issuance Program prices new shares off a Pyth oracle at or below the Nasdaq/NYSE price with a configured discount, circuit breakers and slippage bounds.

venues: No centralised exchange listing for the tokens. Peer-to-peer transfers between allowlisted wallets.

openQuestions: Is the FWDI/HSDT Solana equity token program the same code as the audited Superstate token programs, and has the EQUITY-specific program (and the EVM EquityToken/DIP contracts) had an independent security audit? The published 0xMacro/ChainSecurity audits cover USTB/USCC and the Allowlist; no equity-token audit was located.

Governance of the admin keys. The Solana Allowlist upgrade authority (2ccHdavxJ3eZ4aUy39sHmykFhiKkuvtomyRLRULrwkMA) and each mint authority are on-curve, system-owned addresses with no multisig program account. Turnkey may enforce an off-chain N-of-M policy, but no threshold, quorum or timelock is disclosed anywhere. Single-key compromise would reach mint, freeze, forced-burn and allowlist writes.

Which register wins in a dispute? The DTAA makes the RTA's off-chain Master Securityholder File authoritative and Superstate's record 'subsidiary', while the SEC-filed Galaxy 8-K says Superstate 'records legal ownership onchain in real time' and 'the registered shareholder list of Galaxy updates in real-time'. If the chain and the RTA's file disagree, no document located says which controls, or who bears the loss.

RESOLVED for FWDI and EXOD, open for the rest: FWDI's published CUSIP 349862409 is the ordinary Nasdaq-listed common-stock CUSIP, assigned by Nasdaq when the 1-for-10 reverse split took effect 2024-06-18 (nasdaqtrader.com Equity Corporate Actions Alert #2024-287) — so no separate tokenized tranche. EXOD's 30209R106 is confirmed by Schedule B of the signed agreement. GLXY (36317J209), HSDT (42328V876) and SBET (820014405) were taken from Superstate's own API and not cross-checked against an independent CUSIP source.

Is there a dividend precedent? DTAA Schedule A §4 sets out a full cash/shares/(future stablecoin) dividend path, but FWDI, GLXY, EXOD and HSDT do not pay dividends, so the path has never been exercised. Likewise no split has occurred (multiplier still 1), so the ScaledUiAmount corporate-action mechanism is untested in production.

Has proxy voting actually been exercised by a tokenized holder? Schedule A §3.3 only commits Superstate to 'coordinate with the RTA to enable shareholder communication and proxy material distribution' — no record of a tokenized holder voting at a meeting was found.

Why is HSDT (Solana Company) still at zero supply? The token was deployed 2025-11-14 and the Digital Transfer Agency Agreement is dated 2025-10-17, but the mint supply was 0 on 2026-09-16. Announced but effectively not live; treat HSDT as non-operational for grading.

What is the real ownership dispersion? 481 Token-2022 accounts exist for the FWDI mint, but ~43% of tokenized supply (3,156,493 FWDI, $19.2M) sits in Kamino, and the public asset page shows an 'AdminSeed-Kamino' label — so the holder count overstates independent economic holders.

Why is the public API's circulating-supply exactly 0.1 shares above the on-chain mint supply on FWDI and GLXY but exact on EXOD and HSDT? The 0.1 'AdminSeed-Kamino' position on the FWDI asset page is the likely cause, but nothing states whether that 0.1 is a real share in the register with no token, a display artefact, or an unminted placeholder — and no published reconciliation would reveal which.

RESOLVED: the freeze-authority/permanent-delegate address 2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x is controlled by the Allowlist program, proven on-chain rather than taken from the docs. Transaction 2hYLRFwbxU7DcMxGudfJopFdCT1txbsi4eLa8zAPo47Enp8hyPhLKK6XDbdUFtuHnWFxTuBxYoN1Z3si2dSZFbDy (blockTime 1789052737, i.e. live activity on 2026-09-16) invokes the Allowlist program HFkKyweJDUuGer5KaCst5qZSYD5aapKaD7xzdNaoRtfA, whose inner instructions are Token-2022 getAccountDataSize, System createAccount, initializeImmutableOwner, initializeAccount3 and thawAccount — i.e. the program creates the associated token account with the ImmutableOwner extension and thaws it in one shot, signing as freeze authority via that PDA. Confirms the documented design and confirms ImmutableOwner is applied at the token-account level. What remains open is only the seed derivation (common single seeds did not reproduce the address) and, separately, who controls the program's upgrade authority.

Superstate's fee to the issuer is $1 per year (DTAA §3.1). Is the commercial arrangement documented elsewhere (equity, warrants, platform fees), and does it create an incentive misalignment for a party that also holds forced-burn authority?

keyGovernance.evidence: stocks/findings.md (Superstate on-chain profile, 2026-09-16): re-read 2026-09-17: the per-mint MINT authorities are single funded system-owned addresses with no multisig or timelock visible (FWDI CWdsNnEuCYzxBjjd9dxvhYuatVHY2cGsMNNJcKsGFSqq, 4.574 SOL), but the one shared freeze/permanent-delegate authority 2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x returns null from getAccountInfo - zero lamports, never initialized - so it is a program signer, not a key. 0xMacro states the design: the Admin Authority for the PermanentDelegate is assigned to the Allowlist Program itself; Superstate states only that key management is facilitated by Turnkey. Tension worth noting: the account that actually thaws holder accounts is the upgradeable Allowlist BPF program HFkKyweJDUuGer5KaCst5qZSYD5aapKaD7xzdNaoRtfA (CPI into Token-2022), so the thaw path is program-mediated even though the authority key is not a PDA of a constrained program.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: The Digital Transfer Agency Agreement is explicit: §1.10 'Master Security holder File means the database shareholder record of ownership maintained by the RTA', and §1.8 Superstate keeps only 'Subsidiary Security holder Records'. §1.9 defines Tokenized Shares as book-entry shares 'represented by' tokens. So the authoritative register is the Recordkeeping Transfer Agent's off-chain master file, into which Superstate transmits on-chain activity (Schedule A §2.1). The chain is a near-real-time mirror of a subsidiary record, not the register. Superstate's and Galaxy's marketing says the opposite ('records legal ownership onchain in real time', 'the registered shareholder list of Galaxy updates in real-time'); the executed contract controls. Corroborating: on termination Superstate must 'deliver to Issuer all Subsidiary Security holder Records' and freeze token transfers (§7.5) — the shares survive off-chain.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Both sender and receiver must be on Superstate's Allowlist. Mechanically: the Token-2022 mints carry DefaultAccountState=Frozen, so every newly created token account is frozen and unusable until the Allowlist program (which holds freezeAuthority) thaws it; a transfer to a non-allowlisted wallet therefore cannot settle. Contractually: DTAA Schedule A §3.4 obliges Superstate to program the contracts 'such that Tokenized Shares may only be transferred to or held by digital wallet addresses of persons or decentralized exchange pools on the Allowlist', and §3.5.5.2 reserves the right to refuse transfers to non-allowlisted addresses. Superstate may also 'block or disable access to any Third-Party Services ... which includes our Allowlist at any time' (Terms §7.3).

bearerRedemption.reason: You cannot present the token to a third party and receive the share. Burn-to-book-entry runs entirely through Superstate: you must have an approved, KYC'd Superstate account, send tokens to Superstate's published burn address, and the book-entry balance then appears in your Superstate portfolio; moving to a broker requires a Superstate transfer-authorization form and a DRS transfer coordinated with the RTA. Burning also produces no payout ('Unlike funds, burning equity tokens does not trigger a payout'). A holder without a Superstate account holds a frozen, unusable token.

forcedTransfers.reason: The mints carry a PermanentDelegate (2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x, verified on-chain 2026-09-16), which can move or burn tokens from any account without the holder's signature, and the Allowlist program holds freezeAuthority so any account can be re-frozen. Superstate documents the intent: admin functions include 'forcibly burning an investor's tokens (if required by exogenous legal circumstances, for example)'; 'In the unusual event in which an investor's Allowlist address is compromised, there are procedures in place capable of restoring your investment'; and the Terms note 'Allowlist restrictions and recovery mechanisms in place' for lost or stolen tokenized shares (§6.2). This is the point on which Opening Bell scores where most tokenized-stock wrappers do not.

titleDeed.reason: The token is the registered common share, not a derived or partial right. Galaxy's SEC-filed 8-K: 'These are not derivatives or representations; they are Galaxy Digital Class A Common Stock, with all the rights that confers.' Forward Industries' 10-K: 'All issued shares, regardless of form, represent identical rights.' The Exodus agreement's Schedule B lists the in-scope security as the same class and the same CUSIP (30209R106) as the NYSE American-listed stock, and Superstate publishes the ordinary CUSIP for every tokenized equity. The holder is a holder of record in their own name (name, address, TIN held by Superstate), not a beneficiary behind a nominee.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Tokens are held in the investor's own Solana wallet once that address is allowlisted; the Terms put the private-key risk squarely on the holder ('by using self custody you take on this full responsibility', §6.4–6.5) and warn that self-custodied holders get no SIPC protection. Galaxy's 8-K: available to 'approved KYC'd investors who can hold and transfer them within their own crypto wallets'. Caveat: self-custody is conditional — the account is frozen by default and only Superstate's allowlist makes it usable, and Superstate can re-freeze it.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token's usability depends continuously on Superstate. The Allowlist program is upgradeable (upgrade authority 2ccHdavxJ3eZ4aUy39sHmykFhiKkuvtomyRLRULrwkMA, a single on-curve system-owned address as of 2026-09-16) and is the only thing that can thaw a token account; mint authority is a separate single on-curve Superstate address per instrument. If Superstate stops operating, no new account can be thawed and no new share can be tokenized or burned. The DTAA anticipates exactly this: on termination Superstate will 'freeze the continued ability to transfer Tokenized Shares and coordinate with the RTA to allow holders of Tokenized Shares to redeem them for Certificated Shares or Book-Entry Shares' (§7.5). The SHARE survives Superstate's disappearance; the TOKEN does not.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unambiguous and stated in writing: New York law and exclusive New York jurisdiction (Terms §12; DTAA §16.2), US federal securities law (Securities Act registration statement effective; Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21; Rule 17Ad-17), an SEC-registered transfer agent with a public file number (84-06972), and named arbitration fora (JAMS for investors, AAA for issuers, both seated in New York).

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent is attached to the token. The mint's TokenMetadata additionalMetadata array is empty and its update authority is Superstate's own admin key; there is no attestation hook, no Chainlink Proof-of-Reserve on the equities, no auditor report and no published reconciliation between the on-chain supply and the RTA's master file. What verification exists is contractual and non-public: the issuer, the RTA and regulators have inspection and audit rights over Superstate's Subsidiary Securityholder Records (DTAA §6.2), and the SEC transfer-agent rules apply. The independent RTA is a real second pair of eyes, but its confirmation is not published or attachable on-chain.

aiReady.reason: KYC is directly in the transfer loop. An address can only hold or receive the token after Superstate verifies the Shareholder Information of the person or entity controlling it and clears AML/sanctions screening (DTAA Schedule A §3.4); the Onboarding API exists precisely to submit KYC-verified identity data plus a wallet address. Onboarding also requires a government ID with a real-time image capture and, for individuals, an SSN and date of birth. Note the partial exception: decentralised exchange POOLS can themselves be allowlisted and the Allowlist program exposes a permissionless Thaw instruction, so protocols can integrate — but an autonomous agent still cannot get its own wallet allowlisted. Fails on unconditionalTransfers regardless.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The mechanism and the obligation both exist. Mechanically the PermanentDelegate and the Allowlist program's freeze authority let Superstate move, burn or freeze tokens without the holder. Contractually Superstate documents forced burns 'if required by exogenous legal circumstances'; will not issue where it has 'official notice from any appropriate authority of competent jurisdiction' that issuance is suspended (DTAA §3.5.2); must cooperate with 'regulatory, judicial or other similar requests for shareholder and share information' (§2.3); and the Terms preserve court relief to 'compel compliance with regulatory requirements or valid court orders' (§13.3) and expressly preserve SEC remedies (§13.6). Escheat and lost-holder obligations (Rule 17Ad-17) are handled.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A trade between two already-allowlisted wallets settles without per-trade sign-off, which is a genuine improvement — but the counterparties cannot be chosen freely: both must have been pre-approved by Superstate, and Superstate 'reserves the right to refuse to transfer On chain Eligible Shares to investors or blockchain addresses that are not on the Allowlist' and, separately, 'until it is satisfied that the requested transfer ... is legally authorized' (DTAA §3.5.5.2–3.5.5.3). Buyer-and-seller agreement alone is not sufficient for a valid transfer.

findings.statement: Per-instrument mint authorities (FWDI CWdsNnEuCYzxBjjd9dxvhYuatVHY2cGsMNNJcKsGFSqq; HSDT 7cowcPXxq3dfEKwg2MHmxkneKSNkzKuma8WZTaaZbwh6), and the Allowlist upgrade authority (2ccHdavxJ3eZ4aUy39sHmykFhiKkuvtomyRLRULrwkMA, 2.58 SOL on 2026-09-17) are single funded system addresses with no Squads or other multisig program account. The shared freeze/delegate authority is the exception: it is an uninitialized program signer, so the concentration risk there is the single upgrade authority over the Allowlist program rather than a private key. Superstate states only that key management is facilitated by Turnkey; no N-of-M threshold is disclosed.

findings.statement: The per-mint MINT authorities are funded system-owned keys (FWDI CWdsNnEuCYzxBjjd9dxvhYuatVHY2cGsMNNJcKsGFSqq held 4.574 SOL on 2026-09-17). The shared freeze and permanent-delegate authority is NOT: getAccountInfo on 2Yq4T3mPNfjtEyTxSbRjRKqLf1pwbTasuCQrWe6QpM7x returns null (zero lamports, never initialized), the shape of a program CPI signer, and 0xMacro confirms the design assigns that authority to the Allowlist Program itself. issuers.issuingEntity: Tessera Works Foundation ("TWF"), a Panama foundation, registered office Ricardo Arias Street, Advanced Tower Building, First Floor, Panama City. Each token is issued by its own wholly owned Panama subsidiary: SPX Tessera Issuer Inc. (T-SpaceX), KLSH Tessera Issuer Inc. (T-Kalshi), OPAI Tessera Issuer Inc. (T-OpenAI). The underlying exposure sits one layer further out, in per-company segregated portfolios of a Cayman Islands segregated portfolio company (SPC).
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Panama (foundation and per-token issuer entities); Cayman Islands (SPC segregated portfolios holding the exposure)
issuers.governingLaw: Singapore law, "without giving effect to its principles or rules of conflict of laws". Disputes: SIAC arbitration, sole arbitrator, seat Singapore, English language; Singapore International Commercial Court for related court proceedings.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: Unlicensed and structured to sit outside securities regulation. Docs: "The product carries a non-security legal opinion under Singapore law, confirming it is structured as a loan product, not a capital markets product" and "T-Tokens represent loan participation rights, not securities, though regulatory treatment may vary by jurisdiction." The opinion itself is not published. No Regulation S or other exemption is cited anywhere in the terms.
issuers.holderClaim: An unsecured stablecoin-loan participation right against one named Panama issuer entity, repayable only out of Liquidity Event Proceeds that issuer actually receives, pro rata to the holder's share of the loan series. The terms are explicit that this is purely contractual: the obligation "does not confer on any User any legal, beneficial or other proprietary interest in those Liquidity Event Proceeds, in any PE Investment or in any asset of that Issuer". No equity, voting or dividend rights and no place on the underlying company's cap table.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: No external share custodian is named. Exposure is held in per-company segregated portfolios inside a Cayman Islands SPC, acquired as "direct shares, contracts for shares, or similar instruments tracking company value". Fireblocks provides MPC key management for the token mint/transfer/burn authorities - that is operational key custody of the tokens, not custody of the underlying shares. The independent auditors who attest the portfolio holdings are not named.

custodyVerification.agent: Chainlink SmartData (DataLink) decentralised oracle network, fed by unnamed independent auditors of the Cayman SPC portfolios
custodyVerification.frequency: Chainlink feeds readable on-chain in real time (published on Solana); the underlying audited asset count behind them is "refreshed approximately monthly", so a feed reflects the most recent attested holdings rather than intra-month portfolio changes
custodyVerification.notes: Materially stronger than peers, with two real caveats. (1) The feeds publish ASSET COUNTS, not dollar values - docs: "The values these feeds publish are asset counts - Proof of Reserve - not dollar valuations of the underlying holdings", so a feed at ratio 1.00 says nothing about what the exposure is worth. (2) The attesting auditors are not named and the attestation reports themselves are not published; docs say only that "All auditors involved in signing off on the attestations ... will be shown on this page" (future tense). Crucially, 1:1 here means supply matches verified units - it is NOT a security interest, because the loan is expressly unsecured.

securityInterest.holder: none - no charge, pledge or lien over the underlying shares is granted to holders

redemption.eligibility: Any holder during the Redemption Period, whether the original lender or a subsequent acquirer of the token - the right runs with the token. Excluded Persons (including all US persons) and persons in Excluded Jurisdictions are barred. Note where the screening power sits in the 2026-08-28 Terms: s.2.1(d) attaches identity verification, AML/CFT and sanctions screening to LENDING (accepting a loan and issuing tokens), not to redemption. Redemption is contingent, not on demand: it requires a Liquidity Event (as the Terms define it, the issuer's divestment of all interests in the PE Investment), actual receipt of the proceeds in full by the issuer, and a Redemption Start Date announced by TWF.
redemption.rails: Holder burns the T-Tokens to the Tessera smart contracts to claim the Redemption Amount. Under the Terms (revised 2026-08-28) the Redemption Amount is “denominated in USDC or USDT as the relevant Issuer may determine in its sole discretion” at a fixed 1 USD : 1 USDC / 1 USD : 1 USDT rate. The docs still carry the older, wider wording that “the specific stablecoin is determined by Tessera at its discretion and may not necessarily be the same stablecoin you originally used”; the Terms prevail over the docs by their own wording.
redemption.fees: 0% on acquisition; 0.2% (20 bps) on sells and transfers, enforced on-chain by the Token-2022 transferFeeConfig extension. Fees can be changed by the transfer-fee config authority.

issuers.corporateActions: Everything hinges on a Liquidity Event. The authoritative Terms (revised 2026-08-28) define it narrowly and self-referentially: “divestment by that Issuer of all interests in that PE Investment for cash or stablecoins or equivalent thereof” — no IPO or change-of-control test at all. The docs redemption page still describes the trigger as an IPO on a recognised exchange or a Change of Control (>50% of voting control acquired, or sale/merger), and the Terms prevail in case of discrepancy. Sequence: the segregated portfolio divests, proceeds flow to the issuer entity, the Redemption Amount is denominated in USDC or USDT at the issuer's choice, TWF announces a Redemption Start Date (which must fall within 90 days of the issuer receiving the proceeds in full), and holders burn tokens for a pro-rata share during the Redemption Period — 10am Panama time on the Redemption Start Date to 10pm Panama time on the 90th day thereafter. On expiry the Redemption Amount “shall cease to be claimable by the holder thereof”, is “retained by the relevant Issuer”, and the issuer is “deemed fully and irrevocably discharged”; the docs add that Tessera “reserves the right to forfeit unclaimed proceeds” and “you permanently lose your funds”. Tokens may keep trading on secondary markets until redemption, and if the portfolio is never divested there is no maturity date at all.

pricing.notes: The API publishes a markPrice and a markValuation per token (T-OpenAI 812.79 / $950B, T-Kalshi 413.80 / $14B, T-SpaceX 423.00 / $800B on 2026-09-16), with no disclosed methodology and no external reference market for a private company. Secondary price discovery happens on Solana DEXs (Meteora, Jupiter). There is no continuous mint/redeem arbitrage loop: primary issuance runs through Alpha Vault pro-rata auctions and direct acquisition on the platform, while redemption is unavailable until a Liquidity Event occurs, so the Chainlink PoR feed constrains supply but nothing pins price to the mark.

venues: Tessera platform (direct acquisition with USDC/USDT, 0% fee)
Alpha Vault pro-rata auctions (fair-launch primary distribution)

incidents.summary: Sector-wide risk event affecting Tessera's largest product: Anthropic and OpenAI both warned in May 2026 that the structures used to tokenize their stock are invalid. Anthropic: “we do not permit special purpose vehicles to acquire Anthropic stock and any transfer of shares to an SPV are void under our transfer restrictions”, and a third party selling through “direct sales, forward contracts, tokenized securities, or other mechanisms” is “likely either engaged in fraud or offering an investment that may have no value due to our transfer restrictions”; OpenAI issued a similar warning that unauthorized transactions may violate US securities laws and could result in invalidation of the underlying equity. The coverage was about PreStocks, not Tessera. Tessera's T-OpenAI acquires exposure via “direct shares, contracts for shares, or similar instruments”, and neither the instrument type nor the counterparty is disclosed per portfolio, so it is not publicly determinable whether T-OpenAI's exposure is of a kind OpenAI would recognise. No reporting named Tessera and Tessera published no response found in this research.

openQuestions: Who are the independent auditors behind the Chainlink PoR feeds, and will the attestation reports themselves ever be published? The docs promise the auditors "will be shown" on the transparency page in future tense.

For T-OpenAI specifically: is the exposure direct shares, a contract for shares, or a synthetic? This decides whether OpenAI's May 2026 position that unauthorised SPV/tokenized transfers are void touches Tessera's portfolio at all.

How does a holder rank on insolvency of the Panama issuer entity? The terms are silent, and the loan is unsecured, so the Cayman segregated portfolio protects the assets from the holder as much as from third parties.

Why does the on-chain reality diverge from the docs - no Transfer Hook despite the claim, and a freeze authority that the Authorities & Security table omits? Who controls 7n2PNcDXVDMK2m8dyV9cVPNY7p4jM4ZMHv7TzfibEt8o?

The docs advertise "no KYC" and permissionless global access while the terms exclude US persons plus 17 jurisdiction categories and reserve identity verification. Which governs in practice, and is any geoblocking enforced?
How is markPrice computed? The API publishes it with no methodology, and there is no external reference market.
Note the jurisdictional irony worth flagging on the site: PreStocks lists both Panama and Singapore as Prohibited Jurisdictions - precisely where Tessera is incorporated and whose law governs it.
What happens if a segregated portfolio's exposure is written down between monthly attestations? Supply is not reduced automatically and the feed lags.

The mints carry no permanentDelegate at all, so there is no delegate authority to govern.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: The loan participation is embodied in the token and follows it. The terms give the redemption right to "a holder of those Stablecoin Loan Tokens (whether such holder is the Lender of that Stablecoin Loan or acquiror of those Stablecoin Loan Token)", and redemption is effected by burning the token to the smart contract. There is no separate register of lenders; the Solana mint is the record of who holds the claim.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Nothing sits in the transfer path. The mints carry no transfer hook (despite the docs claiming one), no allowlist, and no defaultAccountState forcing new accounts frozen; docs promise you can "transfer freely to anyone" and describe "permissionless, global participation". The 20 bps transfer fee is a fee, not a gate. The freeze authority is reactive, matching the reactiveCompliance model this flag implies.

bearerRedemption.reason: This is Tessera's strongest feature and what separates it from PreStocks. The terms expressly extend redemption to an "acquiror of those Stablecoin Loan Token", not just the original lender, and it is exercised by burning the token to a smart contract rather than by applying to the issuer for discretionary approval. Qualified: the right is contingent on a Liquidity Event and a 90-day window, US persons and 17 excluded jurisdictions are barred, and the issuer may demand AML information - so it is a bearer right with eligibility screening, not an unconditional one.

forcedTransfers.reason: The mints have a freezeAuthority, which can immobilise a token account, but no permanentDelegate and no clawback - so the issuer cannot move a token to a different owner without the holder's key. That means no token-theft recovery, no recovery of tokens sent to an unreachable address, and no mechanism to vest a deceased holder's tokens in their heirs. Freezing destroys value; it does not reassign it.

titleDeed.reason: Explicitly the opposite. The token is a loan participation, and the terms state the issuer's obligation "does not confer on any User any legal, beneficial or other proprietary interest in those Liquidity Event Proceeds, in any PE Investment or in any asset of that Issuer". Docs: "T-Tokens are not equity. Holders have no ownership, voting, or dividend rights ... and do not appear on its cap table."

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Ordinary Token-2022 mints held in any Solana wallet; no custodial account, and docs advertise use across Solana DeFi (DEX trading, lending, LPing) which presupposes self-custody.

issuerIndependent.reason: The claim is an unsecured obligation of a Panama SPV and is worthless without the operator. Tessera alone declares the Liquidity Event, decides when the Redemption Period opens, and chooses the payout stablecoin; if the window lapses the proceeds are forfeited and the issuer is "deemed released from all obligations". Because the loan is unsecured, holders have no claim on the Cayman portfolio's assets if the issuer fails, and if Tessera simply stopped operating no redemption would ever be declared.

presetJurisdiction.reason: The clearest legal framing of the three issuers. Named issuing entities with a registered address, Singapore substantive governing law with conflict-of-laws expressly disapplied, SIAC arbitration seated in Singapore with the Singapore International Commercial Court as the related court forum, and a disclosed Panama/Cayman two-tier structure. A holder knows exactly whom to sue, where, and under which law.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Independent attestations exist and are attached to the token in machine-readable form: audited asset counts for each Cayman segregated portfolio are refreshed roughly monthly, fed through Chainlink's oracle network, and published as live on-chain SmartData PoR feeds on Solana for all three tokens, so anyone can verify supply against attested units. Weakened by the auditors not being named and the underlying reports not being published, and by the feeds carrying counts rather than valuations.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers yes and tokenSelfCustody yes. Docs are explicit - "Anyone can verify that token supply matches actual asset holdings - no KYC, no intermediaries, no trust assumptions" and "no KYC required" for participation. An agent can acquire, hold and trade T-Tokens; it could not satisfy the terms' eligibility representations or any AML request at redemption.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: A court could order a T-Token transferred, and the operator could not execute it. With only a freeze authority and no permanent delegate or clawback, on-chain enforcement is limited to immobilising a balance - it cannot revert ownership, satisfy a seizure with delivery to a receiver, or effect an inheritance. The terms also nowhere address insolvency ranking or how a court order would be given effect on the ledger.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A DEX or wallet-to-wallet transfer settles on the agreement of buyer and seller alone - no issuer sign-off, allowlist check, or KYC step is in the transfer path, and the redemption right transfers with the token to the acquirer by operation of the terms.

issuers.issuingEntity: unknown - no legal entity is named anywhere in the public documentation. Critically, Ventuals issued no instrument at all: it was a HIP-3 market deployer on Hyperliquid, so there is no issuer of a security or token to identify.
issuers.governingLaw: unknown - no terms of service, governing-law clause or dispute-resolution provision appears in the docs corpus or on the app
issuers.regulatoryStatus: unknown / unlicensed, and structurally different from its peers: because a Ventuals position was a cash-settled derivative referencing a valuation rather than a claim on shares, no SPV, share transfer or securities offering was involved. Press coverage framed this as the category's regulatory workaround - a shift "from tokenized stock structures using special purpose vehicles, which have faced legal challenges, to synthetic perpetuals that may avoid some restrictions but could still face future scrutiny from private companies". No CFTC, SEC or offshore registration, exemption or US-person exclusion was found in any primary source.
issuers.holderClaim: Nothing was owned. A position was a margin position in a Hyperliquid HIP-3 perpetual futures market, cash-settled in USDH. Docs are unambiguous: "Instead of share prices, on Ventuals you trade on whether you think the total valuation of the company is going to go up or down. When you have a position in a company on Ventuals, you do not have any underlying economic ownership in the company - you're merely speculating on its valuation change." Company valuations were divided by 1 billion and quoted as "Valuation Units".
issuers.underlyingCustodian: none - there were no shares, SPV, holding entity or custodian anywhere in the structure. The only asset involved was USDH margin collateral held in the trader's on-chain HyperCore account. USDH is "deployed through Stripe's stablecoin platform (Bridge), fully backed 1:1 by US Treasuries, cash, and cash equivalents managed by BlackRock".

custodyVerification.notes: Nothing to verify by construction - a fully synthetic derivative has no reserve. This is not a disclosure failure but a category difference: where PreStocks and Tessera invite proof-of-reserve questions, Ventuals had no reserve to prove. What was verifiable was the margin system itself: positions, oracle prices and USDH collateral all lived on Hyperliquid and were publicly inspectable on-chain, with oracle prices pushed roughly every 3 seconds.

securityInterest.holder: none - no asset existed to take security over

redemption.eligibility: n/a - positions were never redeemable for shares or any underlying. Exit was by closing the position on the order book, or by automatic cash settlement at wind-down.
redemption.rails: PnL cash-settled in USDH with no USDH/USD conversion. At wind-down all open positions were settled automatically at a frozen mark price with no action required from traders; users then bridged USDH to USDC via the HyperCore USDH/USDC order book or the 1:1 zero-fee HyperEVM bridge through Across Protocol.
redemption.fees: No deposit fees, no withdrawal fees and no cut of native HYPE staking yield on vHYPE - docs: "Ventuals has never earned any fees on vHYPE." Trading fees followed the Hyperliquid HIP-3 venue model.

issuers.corporateActions: n/a - no equity, so no dividends, splits, votes or cap-table events could flow through. The only lifecycle event was the venue's own wind-down, which functioned as a synthetic settlement: effective 9:30am ET 2026-06-15 the OPENAI and ANTHROPIC marks were frozen at their 24-hour TWAPs (mark samples every 5 minutes) and funding rates set to 0, "the fairest settlement mechanic considering that these markets do not have a realtime external reference price". OPENAI halted 10:30am ET 2026-06-15 and settled at $1,341.80; ANTHROPIC halted 11:30am ET 2026-06-15 and settled at $1,618.90. Commodity markets froze to CME prices at 2:20pm ET 2026-06-18 (SOY 2:30pm, WHEAT 3:30pm); index markets froze at 4:00pm ET 2026-06-18 and halted hourly from 4:30pm to 11:30pm ET. vHYPE withdrawals returned HYPE 1:1 plus accrued native staking yield, batch-processed from 10am ET 2026-06-19 and every 24-72 hours thereafter.

pricing.notes: Two-thirds self-referential, and the operator said so. Oracle price = (1/3) x Notice valuation estimate + (2/3) x 2-hour EMA of Ventuals' own mark price, pushed on-chain about every 3 seconds. The external third came from Notice (notice.co), polled at least once a minute, incorporating secondary transactions, secondary bids and offers, fundraising announcements, mutual fund marks, 409A valuations and a comparable public-company set. Mark price was itself an EMA of a liquidity-weighted impact price with a dynamic coefficient k that falls to 0 once the impact price deviates 2% or more from its 1-minute EMA, capping mark movement at 0.125-0.2% per update. The operator designed in room for price discovery deliberately, citing the "IPO pop" phenomenon - but the sunset guide concedes outright that these markets "do not have a realtime external reference price", so no arbitrage could anchor them and the settlement price had to be an internal TWAP. The one external validation point in the sector: a Hyperliquid pre-IPO perp priced Cerebras within 1.3% of its $350 Nasdaq opening price.

incidents.summary: Ventuals announced it was sunsetting and winding down its on-chain pre-IPO markets, with the team folding into an unnamed project in the Hyperliquid ecosystem. Over its run it traded more than $650 million in volume and raised over 500,000 HYPE in community support. This is the decisive fact for grading: the entire product was extinguished at an operator-chosen mark within hours of the announcement, and holders had no instrument that survived it.

incidents.summary: Pre-IPO market settlement executed: marks frozen at 24-hour TWAPs and funding zeroed at 9:30am ET; OPENAI halted 10:30am ET and settled at $1,341.80; ANTHROPIC halted 11:30am ET and settled at $1,618.90. All open positions settled automatically. The operator warned traders against closing early because "liquidity may be thin and the orderbook price may deviate from the mark price TWAP" - an admission that the order book could not be relied on to exit at fair value.

openQuestions: CORRECTION FOR THE EXISTING RECORD: the repo's "Ventuals Pre-IPO" entry is typed "Tokenized Pre-IPO Equity" with tokenStandard "HyperEVM". Ventuals never tokenized equity and issued no pre-IPO token - it deployed HIP-3 perpetual futures markets on Hyperliquid. The record's asset_image also points at a vHYPE logo, which is the HYPE staking vault token rather than any pre-IPO asset. The blockchain field (Hyperliquid) is correct.

CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH PREMISE: Ventuals has no Solana presence - no program, no mint, no Solana deployment at any point. The dossier was requested on the assumption of Solana pre-IPO exposure; the Solana pre-IPO issuers are PreStocks and Tessera.

The record should be marked defunct: all markets were settled and halted in June 2026 and app.ventuals.com now serves only a sunset notice. Consider whether rwa-sonar keeps defunct entries with a status flag or retires them, since a maturity grade on a dead product is misleading either way.
Which Hyperliquid-ecosystem project did the team join? Neither the announcement nor any coverage named it, and it matters for whether these markets return under a new operator.

Was there ever a terms of service, and were US persons excluded? Nothing was found - notable given that this synthetic structure was widely read as the way to sidestep the SPV transfer-restriction problem.
Did any email-signup users lose access by not exporting their Privy wallet before the 2026-09-15 sunset-page deadline?

Note for cross-referencing: Ventuals ran OPENAI and ANTHROPIC markets but not SPACEX in the final period - press attributes the SPACEX pre-IPO perp on Hyperliquid to Trade.xyz, while the Ventuals docs list SPACEX among its own markets. Deployer attribution over time is unresolved.

keyGovernance.evidence: Not applicable: Ventuals never issued a token and never deployed a Solana program. Positions were margin entries in a Hyperliquid HIP-3 perpetual market, so no mint, freeze or delegate authority exists to govern (stocks/findings.md, Ventuals entry).

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Consistent with the existing record. The Hyperliquid HIP-3 order book and margin engine were genuinely on-chain and authoritative for the POSITION, but there was no ownership of any real-world asset for a ledger to record. The referenced companies' cap tables were entirely untouched by anything happening on Ventuals, and the docs say so explicitly: no underlying economic ownership.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: A perpetual futures position is account state in a margin engine, not a bearer instrument. It could not be sent to another address at any price, and could only be entered or exited against the venue's order book. The operator could and did halt trading and force-settle every position.

bearerRedemption.reason: There was nothing to redeem and no custodian to present to. Exposure terminated either by closing on the order book or by the operator's automatic cash settlement in USDH.

forcedTransfers.reason: No token existed to move, so the loss-recovery, theft-recovery and heritability capabilities this flag is about were all structurally unavailable. The venue could liquidate under-margined positions and did force-settle all positions at wind-down, but forced settlement of a derivative is not the ability to reassign ownership of an asset to a rightful owner or heir.

titleDeed.reason: The clearest 'no' of the three issuers, and by design rather than by omission: "you do not have any underlying economic ownership in the company - you're merely speculating on its valuation change." The position referenced a valuation figure, not even a share price.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Consistent with the existing record. Non-custodial in the usual DEX sense - the trader held their own keys and the USDH margin sat in an on-chain HyperCore account they controlled, with permissionless withdrawal. Qualified twice: margin was posted into the venue's margin system rather than sitting free in a wallet, and email signups used Privy embedded wallets that had to be exported before the sunset page went dark.

issuerIndependent.reason: Demonstrated, not merely predicted - the strongest available evidence for this flag anywhere in the pre-IPO category. The operator announced a wind-down and within two hours had frozen the marks, halted the markets and extinguished every pre-IPO position at a price of its own construction. Nothing survived the operator's exit. To its credit the wind-down was orderly and vHYPE depositors were returned HYPE 1:1 plus yield, but orderliness is not independence.

presetJurisdiction.reason: No legal entity, no jurisdiction of incorporation, no governing law, no dispute-resolution clause and no terms of service were found in the docs corpus or on the app. A trader had no identifiable counterparty and no forum.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: No attestation mechanism existed and nothing could be attested, since there was no underlying asset or reserve to link a position to. The nearest third-party input was Notice (notice.co) supplying one-third of the oracle weight - a valuation data vendor, not an attestor of any asset's existence.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers is no, so aiReady is no regardless of KYC. Consistent with the existing record. Worth noting the failure mode was not KYC - no KYC was documented - but the non-transferability of margin positions.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: There was no ownership ledger for a court to correct. The operator could liquidate, halt and force-settle positions, but could not revert ownership, give effect to a seizure by delivering an asset, or vest anything in an heir - because no asset was ever held.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Positions could not be assigned between parties by agreement. Entry and exit ran exclusively through the venue's order book and margin engine, and the operator retained the power to halt trading and settle unilaterally - which it exercised on 2026-06-15.

issuers.holderClaim: The holder owns a bearer debt instrument classified as a tracker certificate — a ledger-based security (Registerwertrecht) giving a claim against the Issuer for a cash Redemption Amount tracking one share of the underlying.
